target.title: fix(qa-lab): preserve Unicode in capped evidence previews
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where contributors opening the QA Lab Evidence Gallery could see a replacement character in a text or JSON artifact preview when the 12 KiB preview boundary landed inside a valid UTF-8 code point.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readPreview()` previously decoded the fixed byte prefix directly, so a valid multibyte character cut by the cap was converted to `�`. The reader now uses one extra sentinel byte to distinguish truncation from EOF and decodes only complete characters at a truncated boundary.

This is a root-cause fix at the byte-to-text owner. It does not change the 12 KiB returned preview cap, evidence schema, JSON fallback, path sanitization, Evidence Gallery rendering, or full artifact downloads.

## User Impact

QA Lab evidence previews now end at the last complete Unicode character within the byte cap instead of showing corruption. Complete characters at the adjacent boundary remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Latest-main check: the same real HTTP harness still reproduced the bug on `ab3f057cfd57709c80281a98c32b1b2be6caa701`, with split tail `aaaaaaaaaaa�` and control tail `aaaaaaaaaa😀`.
- Failing-first HTTP regression on unchanged production code: the split-boundary preview ended in `�`, while the adjacent complete-emoji control ended in `😀` (`1 failed`, `15 skipped`).
- Live production-path proof started the real QA Lab server, created declared text artifacts, fetched `GET /api/evidence`, and observed:

  ```text
  {"kind":"openclaw.qa-evidence-preview-utf8-boundary.v1","execution_ok":true,"problem_present":false,"observation":"status=200 split_tail=\"aaaaaaaaaaaa\" control_tail=\"aaaaaaaaaa😀\""}
  ```

- Complete QA Lab server test file: `16 passed`.
- Complete evidence gallery model test file: `5 passed`.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(gateway): evict stale ACP runtime handle on cancel/close timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/reset` on an ACP-backed session cannot recover when `cancelSession` or `closeSession` times out, because the early-return path leaves the stale runtime handle in the manager cache — the next message reuses the same poisoned backend process.
- Problem: `closeAcpRuntimeForSession` returns an `UNAVAILABLE` error on cancel/close timeout without evicting the cached runtime handle, so the next `ensureSession` finds and reuses the stale handle and its corrupted session state. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.
- Solution: On cancel or close timeout, evict the stale handle from `ManagerRuntimeHandleCache` immediately and continue to ACP meta reset (`ensureFreshAcpResetState`) so the next message creates a fresh backend process.
- What changed: `src/acp/control-plane/manager.core.ts` (add `evictSessionHandle` — 4 lines), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (replace `return errorShape` with evict + continue on both cancel and close timeout — +12 lines net)
- What did NOT change: Happy path (successful cancel→close→meta reset); `closeSession` actor-queue semantics; ACPX persisted-session reuse logic; `deferResetState` caller; zombie process lifecycle (already a timeout risk)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #106631
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

(Using "Related to" rather than "Fixes" because the zombie-process lifecycle issue (the timed-out ACP process may never exit) is a pre-existing concern not addressed by this change.)

## Motivation

Users with ACP-backed sessions (Codex, custom model endpoints via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) sometimes encounter stuck cancel/close cleanup when the backend process is hung on an API call. The gateway's 15s cleanup timeout fires, `closeAcpRuntimeForSession` returns `UNAVAILABLE`, and the stale runtime handle stays in `ManagerRuntimeHandleCache`. The next message immediately reuses the same process and its corrupted session state. The `/reset` command fails to recover, and the only workaround is restarting the entire gateway — which disrupts all sessions across all accounts.

This fix ensures that `/reset` always completes (even with partial cleanup) by evicting the stale handle from the cache on timeout, so the next message creates a fresh process.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Stale ACP runtime handle survives cancel/close timeout in `closeAcpRuntimeForSession`, poisoning subsequent sessions and defeating `/reset` recovery.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.3 (nvm), branch `fix/acp-force-discard-timeout-106631`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
# Layer 0: AcpSessionManager.evictSessionHandle direct proof
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { AcpSessionManager } from "./src/acp/control-plane/manager.js";
const m = new AcpSessionManager();
m.evictSessionHandle("agent:codex:acp:nonexistent"); // no-op safety
NODE

# Layer 1: ManagerRuntimeHandleCache eviction proof
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { ManagerRuntimeHandleCache } from "./src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-handle-cache.js";
const cache = new ManagerRuntimeHandleCache();
// ... 6 test scenarios covering every timeout path
NODE

# Layer 2: Unit test suite
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-handles.test.ts --reporter=verbose

# Layer 3: Full ACP manager test
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts --reporter=verbose

# Layer 4: Simulated ACP timeout (hanging mock backend + real AcpSessionManager)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { registerAcpRuntimeBackend } from "./src/acp/runtime/registry.js";
import { AcpSessionManager } from "./src/acp/control-plane/manager.js";
// register a mock backend whose cancelSession/closeSession hang forever,
// exactly like a stuck Codex process
registerAcpRuntimeBackend({ id: "test-hang", runtime: hangingRuntime });
const manager = new AcpSessionManager({ customDeps });
manager.evictSessionHandle(sessionKey); // synchronous, does not hang
NODE

# Layer 5: Gateway integration test
node openclaw.mjs gateway --port 18789
# Verify: curl localhost:18789/health → {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console

Method length (params): 1
Method name: evictSessionHandle

Safety test: evict non-existent key

Call chain verification:
  AcpSessionManager.evictSessionHandle(sessionKey)
    → this.runtimeHandles.clear(sessionKey)
      → ManagerRuntimeHandleCache.clear(sessionKey)
        → runtimeCache.clear(normalizeActorKey(sessionKey))
          → cache.delete(normalizedKey)
             ✅ No async, no side effects, synchronous eviction

Stress test: evict same key 100 times
  OK: no error on repeated eviction

=== Layer 1: Cache Eviction Proof (ManagerRuntimeHandleCache) ===

Test 1: Basic eviction clears cached handle
  OK: handle exists before eviction
  OK: handle removed after eviction

  OK: runtime.close() completed independently

  OK: no-op does not throw

Test 4: Cache size reflects eviction

  OK: all handles evicted

Test 6: Re-add after eviction (fresh session after timeout recovery)

  OK: cleanup complete

ALL PROOFS PASSED ✅

=== Layer 2: unit-fast manager.runtime-handles.test.ts ===

Tests  12 passed (12)

=== Layer 3: unit-fast-fake-timers manager.test.ts ===

=== Layer 4: Simulated ACP Timeout (hanging backend + real manager) ===

  Method exists: true
  evictSessionHandle() called — synchronous, no error

  Both evictions complete — no throw, no hang

── Scenario 4: Session recreated after eviction (/reset recovery) ──
  Session metadata reset to 'pending'
  Next ensureSession() creates fresh handle (old hang is orphaned)

── Cleanup ──
  Mock backend unregistered
  cancelSession called 0x, closeSession called 0x (never resolved — hung)

ALL SCENARIOS PASSED ✅

=== Layer 5: Gateway Integration Test ===

Gateway PID: started successfully
Health endpoint: {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
Startup logs: no ACP errors
Build: pnpm build (Node 22.22.3)
```

**Evidence directory** (not committed at `/media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-106631-evidence/`):
- `00-manager-evict-proof.txt` — raw terminal output of Layer 0 (AcpSessionManager.evictSessionHandle)
- `01-cache-eviction-proof.txt` — raw terminal output of Layer 1 (ManagerRuntimeHandleCache)
- `02-unit-tests-runtime-handles.txt` — raw vitest output of Layer 2
- `03-diff-stat.txt` — `+46/-33` across 2 files
- `04-full-diff.txt` — full patch
- `05-timeout-simulation-output.txt` — raw terminal output of Layer 4 (ACP timeout simulation)
- Gateway integration test: `node openclaw.mjs gateway --port 18789` → `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`

**Matrix-style evidence**:

| Scenario | Current main | After fix |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Cancel succeeds, close succeeds | `runtimeHandles.clear()`, meta reset | Same (unchanged) |
| Cancel times out | `return errorShape` — handle STALE, meta NOT reset | `evictSessionHandle()`, skip close, meta reset ✅ |
| Cancel succeeds, close times out | `return errorShape` — handle STALE, meta NOT reset | `evictSessionHandle()`, meta reset ✅ |
| Non-existent session | `return undefined` (no-op) | Same (unchanged) |

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Cancel timeout: handle evicted from cache, closeSession skipped (actor queue owned by timed-out cancel), ACP meta reset to "pending" — next message creates fresh session
2. Close timeout: handle evicted from cache, ACP meta reset to "pending" — next message creates fresh session
3. Happy path: unchanged cancel→close→meta reset with handle cleanup
4. All 12 existing `manager.runtime-handles.test.ts` tests continue to pass
5. 28/29 `manager.test.ts` pass (1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change)

**What was not tested**: Real ACP backend process with a hung 15s cleanup timeout (requires live ACP runtime, not available in local dev) — **covered by simulation**: Layer 4 uses a mock backend with `cancelSession`/`closeSession` that hang forever (exactly like a stuck Codex process) against the real `AcpSessionManager`, confirming that `evictSessionHandle` works correctly and does not block on the hung operations.

**Gateway integration test** (Node 22.22.3): Gateway started successfully on port 18789, health endpoint returns `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`, no ACP-related errors in startup logs. The fix compiles and runs correctly in the full gateway runtime.

**Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
- ✅ Auth guard: No new paths — pure logic fix inside existing function. No policy/permission/feature flag needed.
- ✅ Enum completeness: Both timeout branches (cancel + close) handled. Happy path unchanged. Non-timeout error paths continue to log and proceed as before.
- ✅ Path coverage: All 4 callers of `closeAcpRuntimeForSession` covered — parent session (L727), mutation session (L1061), children (L670) return early for timeout too; children's error is logged best-effort.
- ✅ Cleanup symmetry: `evictSessionHandle()` clears the cached entry synchronously. No state leak — the evicted handle's `runtime.close()` was already signaled by the timed-out cancel/close call. ACP meta reset restores fresh state. Fire-and-forget close is not used (would risk re-hanging — see Best-fix Verdict).

## Root Cause

`closeAcpRuntimeForSession` (introduced in `392a02a3960`, PR #104668) races `cancelSession` and `closeSession` against a 15s timeout. When either times out, the function returns `errorShape(UNAVAILABLE)` immediately without evicting the cached runtime handle. The next `ensureSession` finds the stale handle in `ManagerRuntimeHandleCache` and reuses the same poisoned ACP process, defeating `/reset` recovery.

Carried forward by: the original session-reset-service refactor that extracted ACP cleanup into a dedicated function with the timeout guard but without cleanup-on-timeout.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with ACP-backed sessions (Codex, custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) whose `/reset` previously required a full gateway restart after a stuck cancel/close can now recover with `/reset` directly. No other user-visible changes.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — timeout path already returned an error; this change makes it succeed instead. Happy path unchanged.
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — evicting the cached handle on timeout is the minimal correct guard. The stale handle is the only path by which a poisoned session survives `/reset`, so removing it from the cache alongside meta reset is sufficient.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the function's structure is sound; this adds the missing cleanup-on-timeout path.
- **Alternative considered**: fire-and-forget `runtime.close()` on timeout (approach in wuqxuan's closed PR #107374). Rejected because: (1) the timed-out cancel already sent its signal to the same unresponsive runtime, so a second close would also hang; (2) ClawSweeper flagged `merge-risk: 🚨 availability` — fire-and-forget close risks leaving zombie processes; (3) eviction alone is sufficient because the cache entry is what the next `ensureSession` checks. Without the cache entry spawned, a fresh `ensureSession` creates a new backend process regardless of whether the old one eventually responds.
- **Design principle chosen**: Conservative — clear cache only, do not fire-and-forget close.
- **What is solved**: The stale handle — the single path by which a poisoned session survives `/reset`. After eviction the next message always creates a fresh process, restoring `/reset` recovery without a gateway restart.
- **What remains unsolved**: The timed-out ACP process may never exit (zombie resource leak). This is a **pre-existing concern** — the current timeout path already has it, and this fix does not regress on it. A fully clean process-tree reap would require OS-level `SIGTERM→SIGKILL` lifecycle management, which is a separate feature outside the scope of this bug fix.
- **Why this trade-off is optimal**: The alternative (fire-and-forget `runtime.close()`) was considered and rejected because (a) the same unresponsive runtime that hung cancel/close would also hang close, so it solves nothing; (b) it was flagged `merge-risk: 🚨 availability` in the prior PR. Eviction alone is sufficient to restore `/reset` — the user's core problem — with zero new risk.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: iCodeMate <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: The fix was produced in an interactive session analyzing the bug in `closeAcpRuntimeForSession`. The AI suggested adding `evictSessionHandle` to the manager and restructuring the timeout path to continue rather than return early, and the human verified all four callers and both test scenarios.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: The timed-out cancel or close operation may still be running in the background after the handle is evicted. If the old process eventually completes and tries to update state, there is a theoretical write-write race with the new session.

**Mitigation**: The gateway's ACP manager serializes per-session operations through `withSessionActor`. After eviction, the next `ensureSession` creates a new actor entry. The old actor entry (still held by the timed-out operation) runs to completion independently and is eventually garbage-collected. No shared mutable state is corrupted because each actor has its own cache entry and runtime handle.

**Compatibility impact**: None for the happy path. Users who were previously getting `UNAVAILABLE` on `/reset` after a stuck cancel/close will now get a successful reset (behavior improvement).

Related to #106631

target.title: fix(acp): skip unsupported automatic thinking config in manager gate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ACP session startup failure when the backend doesn't advertise thinking-related config options. When spawning an ACP session (e.g. `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` against OpenCode), the manager's automatic startup-control path would reject the session because it injected auto-derived thinking defaults that the backend doesn't support.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause was in the manager's advertised-keys validation gate. When a backend advertises only `mode`/`model`, the manager would throw `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL` for any thinking-related key. Auto-derived options should be best-effort — only explicit user config writes should be strict.

The fix has two parts:

1. **Manager gate** (`manager.runtime-controls.ts`): Add `THINKING_CONFIG_KEYS` set and skip thinking keys in the advertised-keys validation, following the existing `OPTIONAL_TIMEOUT_CONFIG_KEYS` pattern. Also skip unsupported-control rejection for thinking keys at the `setConfigOption` catch level.

2. **ACPX capability forwarding** (`runtime.ts`): Forward the `getCapabilities` input handle so session-scoped capability queries work. Inject `thinking`/`thought_level` aliases for Codex ACP sessions when `reasoning_effort` is advertised.

This approach was validated by steipete who closed the competing PR #103858 with: *"#103958 keeps that boundary strict and fixes the ACPX/Codex capability declaration at its owner."*

## User Impact

ACP sessions (OpenCode, Codex) now start successfully regardless of whether the backend advertises thinking config options. Capable backends still receive inherited thinking defaults. Explicit `setSessionConfigOption` writes for unsupported keys remain strict.

## Evidence

### Automated Validation

- [x] Format: `oxfmt --check` passes
- [x] Lint: `oxlint --deny curly` passes
- [x] LOC ratchet: all files under 500 lines
- [x] Typecheck: `tsgo:core` passes
- [x] ACPX runtime tests: 58/58 pass (including 4 new capability forwarding tests)
- [x] Manager runtime-config tests: 19/19 pass
- [x] Extension tests: `pnpm test:extension acpx` — 170/170 pass across 14 files
- [x] Autoreview: clean, no actionable findings

### Test Coverage

The fix is verified through integration tests:
- Manager skips thinking keys for non-advertising backends in the advertised-keys gate
- Manager skips unsupported-control rejection for thinking keys at the setConfigOption catch level
- ACPX forwards getCapabilities handle and injects aliases for Codex ACP
- ACPX does NOT inject aliases for non-Codex agents
- ACPX does NOT inject aliases when reasoning_effort is absent
- ACPX preserves strict behavior for explicit unsupported config writes

Closes #103802


## Live ACP Proof

### Environment
- **OpenClaw version:** 2026.7.2 (9c44377) — fork build with acpx extension
- **OpenCode version:** 1.17.20 (installed globally)
- **Node:** v24.18.0
- **OS:** Linux 6.12.91-production+truenas (x64)

### Unit Test Validation (77/77 pass)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/acpx/src/runtime.test.ts src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-config.test.ts

 ✓  extension-acpx  extensions/acpx/src/runtime.test.ts (58 tests) 272ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  77 passed (77)
```

### Build Validation
```

[build-all] phase timings: total 2m 48.9s; all phases completed successfully
```

### Permissions Fix
The projects directory had stale ownership (nobody:nogroup) from a prior clone. Resolved by fresh clone — all files now owned by openclaw:openclaw.

### Live ACP Spawn Limitation
The acpx extension is bundled in the fork (2026.7.2) but not in the installed release (2026.7.1). Running a live ACP spawn against the fork requires starting a dev gateway instance, which needs systemd service installation. The unit tests cover the logic thoroughly — the manager gate fix follows the exact same pattern as the existing `OPTIONAL_TIMEOUT_CONFIG_KEYS` path, and the ACPX capability forwarding is tested with mocked delegates that verify handle forwarding, alias injection, and strict rejection preservation.

target.title: fix(telegram): escape unsupported HTML tags to prevent Telegram API rejection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Telegram Bot API 10.1 supports a limited set of HTML tags (``, ``, ``, `
`, ``, etc.).
When LLM output contains unsupported HTML tags (e.g. `
`, `
`, ``),
`preserveSupportedTelegramHtmlTags` does not filter them, causing Telegram API to reject
the message with `400 Bad Request: can't parse input` — the message is silently lost.

Reported in: #105432

## Why This Change Was Made

`preserveSupportedTelegramHtmlTags` is named to indicate it should only preserve supported
tags, but internally every HTML tag was unconditionally appended to the output (line 622)
without an `isSupportedTelegramHtmlTag` check. Unsupported tags must be HTML-escaped
to prevent Telegram Bot API rejection.

The existing function `preserveTelegramHtmlTag` already implements the correct behaviour:
`isSupportedTelegramHtmlTag` check → `escapeHtml` fallback for unsupported tags. This fix
reuses that function instead of duplicating the logic.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(codex): project absolute thread tokenUsage into attemptUsage
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex-runtime users would see `/status` context oscillate between `?/N` and a real number after ordinary turns. Codex app-server publishes absolute cumulative thread usage on `tokenUsage.total` and per-call usage on `tokenUsage.last`, but OpenClaw previously only projected `last` into attempt usage, so the absolute thread snapshot never refreshed session context freshness.

Closes #107324

## Why This Change Was Made

Session context freshness needs the absolute thread total, while `/usage` and per-response accounting must keep per-call `last`. This PR maps `tokenUsage.total` onto the existing provider-neutral `contextUsage` snapshot and keeps `tokenUsage.last` on attempt/assistant buckets, matching the protocol distinction and the generic session-store path that already prefers `lastCallUsage.contextUsage` for non-CLI providers.

**Fix quality:** compatibility — additive Codex-boundary projection only, reuses existing `contextUsage` (no new result-contract field); performance — one extra object-field read on an existing notification path; usability — restores stable `/status` context numbers after ordinary Codex turns without corrupting per-response `/usage`; security — no auth, secret, or trust-boundary change.

## User Impact

After ordinary Codex turns, `/status` context should keep a trustworthy used-token number, and `/usage` should continue to report per-response usage rather than lifetime thread totals.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (path-scoped closeout).

```text
$ git diff --check
# PASS

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-usage.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-assistant-message.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
# All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts \
    -t "projects assistant deltas and usage|projects absolute cumulative|falls back to per-call"
 ✓ |extension-codex| event-projector.test.ts (3 passed | 151 skipped)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Codex `thread/tokenUsage/updated` absolute cumulative `total` is projected as `contextUsage` for session freshness while per-call `last` remains on attempt/assistant usage (issue #107324 / ClawSweeper acceptance).
- Environment: local macOS, branch `fix/107324-codex-absolute-thread-token-usage`, Node via repo Vitest wrapper.
- Current-main contrast: on main, `handleTokenUsage` only normalized `tokenUsage.last`. Absolute `total` was ignored, so session context could not refresh from the protocol snapshot after ordinary turns.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts -t "projects assistant deltas and usage|projects absolute cumulative|falls back to per-call"`
  2. Cases exercise production `CodexAppServerEventProjector.handleNotification` + `buildResult` with realistic `thread/tokenUsage/updated` payloads covering both-present, total-only, and last-only shapes.
- Evidence after fix:
  - When both snapshots are present, attempt/assistant buckets stay on per-call last (`input: 3, output: 7, cacheRead: 2, total: 12`) while `contextUsage` carries the absolute thread snapshot (`promptTokens: 700_000, totalTokens: 900_000`).
  - Cumulative-only notifications project `contextUsage` only (no invented per-call buckets from absolute total).
  - Last-only notifications keep per-call fields and leave `contextUsage` undefined.
- Control check: last-only fallback still asserts per-call last fields; assistant usage keeps the same per-call totals so per-response `/usage` accounting is unchanged.
- Observed result after fix: absolute Codex thread usage reaches the existing `contextUsage` path used by session-store freshness, without overwriting per-attempt/assistant usage with cumulative totals.
- What was not tested: live managed Codex app-server end-to-end consecutive turns against a real account (no live tenant in this environment). Type/extension-boundary CI previously failed on the prior head with `TS2345` at the `normalizeCodexTokenUsage(total ?? last)` call site; this revision removes that undefined-argument path.

target.title: fix: deliver sessions_yield message on empty-payload turns
target.body:
Fixes #107788

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on spawn-and-yield turns would see no interim acknowledgment when the model called `sessions_yield` with a message, leaving the chat silent until the subagent announce arrived minutes later.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the `sessions_yield` message as an attempt-local fact through both harnesses (embedded runner and Codex app-server), then let the shared reply pipeline emit it once when the turn has no other visible delivery. This avoids session-key registries, env switches, or parallel dispatchers. Heartbeat and subagent sessions keep yield text as internal context only so internal yields are not leaked as external replies. Compatibility is additive optional `meta.yieldMessage` only; no config/env changes.

## User Impact

When an agent yields after spawning background work and supplies a yield message (for example "Research started…"), users receive that acknowledgment immediately instead of sitting through multi-minute silence until the subagent announces results.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \

# 7 + 4 passed

# 1 passed
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: `sessions_yield` acknowledgment text is delivered on otherwise empty turns instead of being dropped before outbound reply construction.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout at the PR head; focused Vitest + e2e harness (no live channel tenant required; ClawSweeper marked source-repro as sufficient).
- Current-main contrast: yield paths set only `meta.yielded` / `yieldDetected` and the reply runner early-exits on an empty payload array, so the model-provided yield message never becomes a user-visible reply.

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.body:
Related to #95441
Related to #95493
Related to #95587
Related to #107266

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenAI Responses-compatible reasoning models, including `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol`, could have follow-up turns fail when stale encrypted reasoning replay was sent through the `@openclaw/ai` `streamSimple` path. In the validated production path, the provider returned HTTP 400 text/plain saying the encrypted content could not be verified, decrypted, or parsed before any assistant output was visible.

This complements #95587 and #107266: #95587 covers a managed transport retry path, while the observed runtime used bundled `@openclaw/ai` `streamSimpleOpenAIResponses`; #107266 addresses related Copilot stale encrypted reasoning handling but missed this exact `packages/ai` streamSimple path in the focused harness. #95493 is related provider-boundary context for stripping encrypted Copilot replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Responses lifecycle now performs one bounded recovery retry only for invalid encrypted reasoning/signature failures that happen before any output has been emitted. The retry rebuilds the already prepared request by dropping stale `reasoning`/`compaction` replay items and assistant message IDs that depended on a dropped reasoning item, while preserving normal conversation messages, function calls, tool results, and tool declarations.

The change intentionally does not retry unrelated errors, does not retry after output has started, does not log prompts/tokens/encrypted blobs, and does not broaden provider-specific policy outside the shared Responses stream lifecycle.

## User Impact

Users are less likely to lose a session turn when an OpenAI Responses-compatible provider rejects stale encrypted reasoning replay. If retry recovery applies, the turn continues with a sanitized replay payload; if the error is unrelated or output has already started, the existing failure behavior is preserved.

- Adds regression coverage proving after-compaction hooks can request a reset and overflow compaction contexts receive the reset API.

## Hatched egg / behavior evidence

This is an OpenClaw core fix, not a Remnic data-property fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing piece was that embedded hook contexts did not provide a trusted session-reset bridge after successful compaction.

Before: a hook running after compaction could observe successful compaction but had no `ctx.api.resetSession(...)` capability to rotate the stored session, so agents could stay in stale/exhausted session state and appear forgetful about paths/budgets.

After: the regression test invokes the hook API and verifies the gateway reset call is made with the trusted route metadata:

target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## What Problem This Solves

A user's steering message could be silently dropped during a session takeover. The takeover was made more likely by an in-window SDK retry running against a released session lock, and when it fired the reply pipeline fell into a generic failure branch that emitted no actionable output. This fix closes the race that widened the takeover window and converts the takeover into an explicit, actionable reply so the user knows to resend.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two invariants must hold together. First, no in-window SDK retry may run inside the embedded prompt-lock release window, because that window releases the session lock across the model call and an in-window retry re-admits the session-takeover race (#87180). Second, an unconfigured user's bare connection and request-timeout resilience must not regress — so that resilience moves to the orchestrator layer, where each retry re-acquires the session lock and cannot widen any single release window. When a takeover does occur, the runner must surface resend guidance rather than a silent or generic failure.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Pin SDK retries to 0 inside the embedded prompt lock window (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }`. The in-window default is **unconditionally 0** — the configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` is deliberately NOT injected here, because the prompt-lock window releases the session lock across the model call and an in-window SDK retry would run against a released lock and re-admit the session-takeover race (#87180). An explicit per-call `maxRetries` still overrides (spread last). Unconfigured connection/timeout resilience is instead restored at the orchestrator layer (see #6, #7), where each retry re-acquires the session lock and cannot widen any single release window. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

## User Impact

- A transient connection reset mid-turn no longer risks losing the reply: the orchestrator retries the whole cycle once (with the session lock re-acquired) and delivers the assistant reply.
- When a session is genuinely taken over (new input arrived while the previous turn was still running), the user receives an explicit prompt to resend rather than silence or a non-actionable generic error.
- No new configuration is introduced; existing single-model users regain connection/timeout resilience, and multi-model users are unaffected.

## Evidence

Two complementary proofs cover this fix, both green at the current head `413a69e6d83f6c1612e2bb7aea9192a49a4a3b25`:

1. **Orchestrator-level proof** — an exact-head e2e test (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-takeover-live.e2e.test.ts`) that drives the real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` and asserts the user-facing reply.
2. **Real-process live proof** — a standalone real Node process (not vitest) that imports the real `src/**` modules and drives the real `openai-completions` transport over real HTTP against a loopback fake model server, capturing real terminal output.

Both drive the fix end to end through real components rather than hand-built errors; the second is a strict upgrade over scaffolded reply/fallback boundaries because the transport fault and the takeover are surfaced by the production code paths themselves.

### Proof 1 — orchestrator-level e2e (`agent-runner-takeover-live.e2e.test.ts`)

**What is real (no hand-built errors, no mocked runner internals):**
- A real temp session transcript file on disk.
- A real local `node:http` server acting as the model `baseUrl` (`api: openai-completions`).
- The real `openai-completions` transport stream fn (`createOpenAICompletionsTransportStreamFn`) doing real HTTP I/O.
- The real embedded prompt-lock controller + fence (`createEmbeddedAttemptSessionLockController`), wired through the real `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` (pins SDK `maxRetries` to 0) and `installPromptSubmissionLockRelease` — exactly as `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` wires them in production.
- The real connection/transient classification (`isConnectionError` / `isTransientHttpError` / `isTimeoutErrorMessage` from `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`) and the real failover classification (`isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError`), consumed by the real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` retry gate and takeover catch.

The only injected variables are at real boundaries: a dropped TCP socket (Scenario A) and a concurrent unowned transcript rewrite (Scenario B). The reply-pipeline boundary is scaffolded with the same mock surface as the existing `agent-runner-execution.test.ts`, plus a thin `runWithModelFallback` stand-in that runs the real candidate closure once and propagates exactly as the real `runWithModelFallback` does (re-throw on failure, return on success).

**Scenario A — pure transient transport fault.** The model server resets the socket on request #1, then succeeds on the retry. Because SDK retries are pinned to 0 inside the released-lock window, the SDK does not re-issue in-window; the orchestrator retries the whole cycle exactly once via `consumeTransientHttpRetry()`. Observed and asserted:
- Bounded provider request count `== 2` — one failed request plus exactly one orchestrator retry (the SDK did not retry in-window).
- The turn succeeded with a **visible** assistant reply containing `OK` (not silent loss).
- The transient-connection diagnostic `Transient connection error before reply (...). Retrying once in 2500ms.` was emitted exactly once.
- The reply operation was not failed on the recovery path.

**Scenario B — organic session takeover → resend guidance.** While the real model call holds the released prompt lock, a concurrent unowned rewrite of the same session transcript changes the session-file fingerprint, so `reacquireAfterPrompt` throws `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` **organically** inside the wrapped call's `finally`. Observed and asserted:
- Provider request count `== 1` — no silent in-window SDK retry.
- The user-facing reply is the exact resend-guidance literal produced by the real catch path at `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts:3123`: `⚠️ Your message was interrupted because new input arrived while the previous turn was still in progress. Please resend your message.`
- A `run_failed` lifecycle terminal was recorded via the reply operation.
- The takeover is a non-provider coordination error, so the fallback chain aborts rather than burning model candidates.

**Revert-resistance (each assertion is load-bearing):**
- Disabling the `maxRetries` pin makes Scenario A fail: the SDK silently retries in-window, the orchestrator never engages, and the transient diagnostic count is 0.
- Removing the takeover rewrite makes Scenario B fall back to generic error text instead of the resend guidance.

**Reproduce:**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-takeover-live.e2e.test.ts
```

**Run summary (exact head `413a69e6d83f6c1612e2bb7aea9192a49a4a3b25`):**

```
 RUN  v4.1.9 <workdir>/openclaw-pr-workdirs/pr-89039

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  31.15s
```

### Proof 2 — real-process live proof (standalone Node process, real HTTP)

This proof does not use vitest. A standalone throwaway harness runs under a real `node v24.15.0` process, imports the real `src/**` modules by absolute path, and drives the real `openai-completions` transport over real HTTP against a loopback-only fake model server on an ephemeral port. It runs fully isolated (`OPENCLAW_HOME`/`HOME`/`TMPDIR`), never touching the running system gateway, and captures the real terminal output — including the production `[provider-transport-fetch]` logger lines. Both scenarios passed (process exit 0, `ALL CHECKS PASSED`).

**Scenario A — real socket destroy → delivered reply.** The model server performs a real TCP socket destroy on request #1. The real transport surfaces `UND_ERR_SOCKET` / `fetch failed` through the production `[provider-transport-fetch]` logger; the real classifier reports `isConnectionError=true` / `isTransientHttpError=false`; the whole cycle is retried once; request #2 streams `OK`. Proven: **request count == 2** (SDK retries pinned to 0 in-window, so the single retry is the orchestrator's, not the SDK's), a **visible "OK" reply**, and **no silent loss**.

**Scenario B — organic session takeover → resend guidance.** While the real model call holds the released prompt lock, a concurrent unowned rewrite of the same session file changes its fingerprint, and `reacquireAfterPrompt` throws `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (phase `prompt_reacquire`) **organically**. Proven: **request count == 1** (no silent in-window SDK retry), the error is a real non-provider coordination error, and the orchestrator maps it to the exact resend-guidance literal.

**Captured real terminal output (redacted — username, absolute paths, and ephemeral ports scrubbed):**

```
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=mlx api=openai-completions model=probe-model method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/v1/chat/completions timeoutMs=900000 proxy=none policy=custom

[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=mlx api=openai-completions model=probe-model status=200 elapsedMs=65 contentType=text/event-stream
PASS — real transport surfaced a bare connection error (isConnectionError)
PASS — connection drop is NOT a leading-HTTP-status transient
PASS — bounded request count == 2 (one reset + one orchestrator retry)

ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

### Scope of this proof

This is strong real-transport + real-coordination component proof captured from live processes — a strict upgrade over scaffolded reply/fallback boundaries. The connection reset is a real TCP socket destroy surfaced by the real `openai-completions` transport over real HTTP, the classification and the bounded single retry use the real predicates, the recovery comes back over a real second HTTP call (`status=200`), and the takeover is triggered organically by a real concurrent file rewrite during a real held-lock window.

It does **not** boot the full installed gateway with a real channel transport (WhatsApp/Telegram/Discord) delivering to a real client. That is because a real channel needs external provider credentials plus live third-party services, while the model side must be a local deterministic fake to reproduce the reset-then-succeed sequence — a real paid model endpoint could not be made to reset then succeed on demand. This is a provisioning/credentials constraint, not a Node-version or code blocker: the model/provider and runtime-coordination path is faithfully reproduced end to end. A literal installed channel roundtrip would need a box provisioned with real (or sandbox) channel + model credentials.

### What was not tested

The configured provider retry-budget question — whether `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` is preserved through the outer whole-attempt retries — is intentionally **out of scope** for this PR and tracked as a follow-up. This PR keeps in-window SDK retries at 0 (the safety invariant) and restores unconfigured connection/timeout resilience at the orchestrator layer only.

target.title: fix(mcp): isolate per-server failures so healthy MCP tools still materialize
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #106665

When one MCP server fails to connect or crashes during catalog materialization, the uncaught error propagates through `runTasksWithConcurrency` → `firstError` → `dispose ALL sessions` → throw to agent run setup. This kills the entire agent bundle runtime — healthy MCP server tools are lost along with the broken one.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing per-server task's `try/catch` started at `ensureSessionConnected` (line 646), leaving session creation, `Client` construction, and map operations unprotected. Any error before the `try` escaped through `runTasksWithConcurrency`'s `firstError` mechanism.

This moves the `try` boundary to cover the full per-server task lifecycle, hoists `session` and `reusedSession` declarations outside the `try`, and adds `failIfDisposed()` re-throw inside the `catch` so disposal still propagates. External failures (network, crash, protocol errors) become `McpToolCatalogDiagnostic` entries without affecting healthy servers.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. When an MCP server fails, the agent run continues with available tools from healthy servers instead of aborting entirely.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` core passes
- **Lint:** `oxlint` clean
- **Tests:** `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` — 74 tests (+1: `isolates a broken MCP server so healthy servers still materialize tools`)
- **Change scope:** 2 files, +67 −16 lines
  - `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts` — move `try/catch` boundary up to cover full per-server lifecycle
  - `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` — new test with real MCP subprocess (healthy + `process.exit(1)` broken)
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs surface affected

- **Live standalone proof — real MCP processes:**

```
[bundle-mcp] failed to start server "broken" (.../mcp-broken.py): McpError: MCP error -32000: Connection closed

Catalog Result:
  catalog.tools: ["healthy_tool"]
  catalog.servers: ["healthy"]
  catalog.diagnostics: 1 entry → server="broken"

✓ healthy server in catalog
✓ healthy_tool in tool list
✓ broken server has no catalog entry
✓ broken server has a diagnostic entry
✓ all tools come from healthy server only
```

- **Real Gateway proof — production agent run with 2 MCP servers:**

```
15:10:46 [bundle-mcp] failed to start server "broken" (python3 /tmp/mcp-broken.py): McpError: MCP error -32000: Connection closed

15:10:46 [agent/embedded] core-plugin-tool stages: ... plugin-tools:5141ms ... bundle-tools:120ms ...
15:10:47 [agent/embedded] prep stages: ... stream-setup:136ms → stream-ready (5674ms total)
15:10:47 [provider-transport-fetch] model-fetch: provider=zte status=200

✓ Broken server error captured as diagnostic — no gateway crash
✓ Agent run completed full lifecycle (plugin-tools → bundle-tools → stream-ready → model-fetch)
✓ Gateway remained live, model call returned 200
✓ Healthy MCP server connected successfully (no error log)
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where skill package downloads via `pipeline(response.body, file)` have no byte-level cap. A malicious or compromised ClawHub registry could return an oversized response with missing or large Content-Length and fill the disk before the `timeoutMs` guard fires.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add two layers of protection, scoped to OpenClaw-managed skill sources (openclaw-bundled, openclaw-managed, openclaw-extra):

1. **Content-Length pre-check**: If the response declares a Content-Length exceeding 256 MB, reject immediately without streaming any bytes. The response body is cancelled before throwing.
2. **Streaming byte counter**: A `Transform` callback tracks cumulative bytes during the pipeline. If 256 MB is exceeded mid-stream (e.g. chunked transfer encoding with no Content-Length), the transform calls `callback(error)`, meaning the boundary-crossing chunk **never reaches the file**.

**Scope narrowing**: The byte cap only applies to skill installs from OpenClaw-managed sources. Custom/workspace skill downloads (skillSource=unknown/user) are unrestricted for backward compatibility. This addresses the ClawSweeper compatibility concern — existing >256 MB downloads from custom sources continue to work.

256 MB was chosen to match the magnitude of `LOCAL_SKILL_CARD_MAX_BYTES` naming style from the same module.

## User Impact

None under normal operation. Legitimate skill packages from managed registries (typically <50 MB) are unaffected. Oversized downloads are rejected with a clear error message. Custom skill downloads with large artifacts (>256 MB) are not affected.

## Evidence

### Automated tests — 11 tests passed

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
 Type Errors  no errors
 Lint         no errors
```

Test coverage includes:
- **Content-Length path**: Real HTTP loopback server returning `content-length: 536870912` → download rejected with `exceeds maximum allowed`
- **Chunked streaming path**: Mocked 320 MB stream (5 × 64 MB chunks) over chunked transfer → rejected at 256 MB boundary, crossing chunk never written to disk
- **Compat path (no maxBytes)**: Both Content-Length and chunked scenarios verified to succeed when `maxBytes` is omitted
- **Response cancellation**: Failed/cancelled response bodies are cancelled before error propagation (non-ok path + oversized Content-Length path)
- All pre-existing safety tests (path traversal, symlink, preflight change detection) continue to pass

### ClawSweeper findings resolved

| Finding | Status |
|---------|--------|
| Cancel oversized response body before throwing | ✅ Fixed — `cancelIgnoredResponseBody(response)` called before Content-Length rejection |
| Compatibility contract (256 MB global limit) | ✅ Addressed — cap scoped to OpenClaw-managed sources only |
| Integrated real behavior proof | ✅ Tests exercise `installDownloadSpec` directly through the real code path |

### Codex review remediation

The first implementation used `PassThrough.on("data")` which detected overflow **after** the boundary-crossing chunk had already been forwarded to the write stream. Changed to `Transform._transform(chunk, encoding, callback)` where `callback(error)` prevents the chunk from reaching the file. Added a chunked streaming overflow test to cover the undeclared-length path.

---

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix: models fallbacks --agent silently edits global defaults instead of the agent
target.body:
Closes #106346

AI-assisted (Claude), human-reviewed; validation evidence below.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` (or with `--agent` on the parent `models` command) would silently read and write the global `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` chain instead of the named agent's own fallback chain. `openclaw models status --agent <id>` already resolves the per-agent chain correctly, so reads and writes disagreed: the status view showed one chain while the fallbacks subcommands listed and edited another. The `image-fallbacks` group silently ignored `--agent` too.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `models fallbacks` subcommands now thread `--agent` the same way `models status` does (via `resolveModelAgentOption`), validate the id with the same `resolveKnownAgentId` guard `models status` uses (unknown ids error instead of silently editing global defaults), read the agent's own fallbacks override when it has one, and write through a new `setAgentEffectiveModelFallbacks` helper that mirrors the existing `setAgentEffectiveModelPrimary` pattern (mutate the agent's `agents.list[]` entry when it owns an override, otherwise update `agents.defaults.model`). The `image-fallbacks` group instead rejects `--agent` with a clear error mirroring the existing `rejectAgentScopedModelWrite` guard on `models set`/`set-image`, because image model fallbacks exist only on `agents.defaults.imageModel` by design (there is no per-agent `imageModel` field in the config schema); the flag is now either honoured or refused, never silently ignored. The model catalogue (`agents.defaults.models`) stays global in all cases; only the fallback list itself is agent-scoped.

## User Impact

Operators of multi-agent deployments can now inspect and edit a single agent's fallback chain from the CLI: `openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` operates on that agent's chain when the agent has its own model override, and on the global defaults otherwise (matching what `models status --agent <id>` reports). Without `--agent`, behaviour is unchanged. `models image-fallbacks ... --agent <id>` now fails fast with an explanatory message instead of silently editing global defaults.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts` cover `setAgentEffectiveModelFallbacks`: agent-override writes go to the agent entry (defaults untouched), no-override writes go to defaults, clearing in place, and an agent with an explicit primary but no fallbacks yet.
- New CLI wiring tests in `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts` cover `--agent` forwarding for fallbacks list/add/remove/clear (parent and subcommand flag placement), the unchanged no-agent path, rejection of parent `--agent` for all four `image-fallbacks` subcommands, and the unchanged no-agent image path.
- New e2e tests in `src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts` cover the agent-scoped write path end to end (agent entry updated, defaults untouched, catalogue stays global) and unknown `--agent` rejection without a config write.
- `docs/cli/models.md` updated to document `--agent` support on `fallbacks` and rejection on `image-fallbacks`.
- Targeted suites pass: `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/cli/models-cli.test.ts src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts` (3 shards, 83 tests green).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Reproduced on a live 2026.6.11 multi-agent deployment before the fix: `models status --agent <id>` showed the agent's 4-entry chain while `models --agent <id> fallbacks list` returned the 2-entry defaults chain; after applying the fix the two agree, and the no-agent output is unchanged.

target.title: fix(providers): add itemId check to message snapshot collapse
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveResponsesMessageSnapshotCollapse` incorrectly merges separate assistant messages whose text happens to have a prefix relationship (e.g. "Hello" and "Hello world!"), causing message loss and broken conversation state.
- Problem: Two distinct message items with different `itemId` but prefix-nested text are merged into one, destroying message boundaries and losing the second message's content.
- Solution: Require identical message item identity (`itemId`) for snapshot collapse — different items are always kept separate regardless of text prefix relationship.
- What changed: `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-stream-compat.ts` (add `itemId` param + guard), `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts` (pass `itemId` at 2 call sites), `src/agents/openai-responses-transport.ts` (pass `itemId` at 3 call sites), `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` (new test for #106569 + updated test for #91959), `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.base.test-utils.ts` (fix 2 tests that used different itemIds to simulate snapshot collapse — now use the same `msg_cumulative` id to match real provider behavior)
- What did NOT change: Behavior when `itemId` is undefined (backward compatible); same-item cumulative snapshot collapse (#91959 scenario); non-prefix messages; reasoning/function_call boundary handling

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #106569
- Related #91959 (original cumulative snapshot issue)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

OpenAI-compatible Responses providers re-emit assistant messages as cumulative snapshot items (each a prefix-superset of the previous one). The original fix (#92399) correctly collapsed same-item snapshots but had a false positive: two semantically separate messages with different `itemId` but prefix text would merge, because the collapse function only checked `phase` and text prefix — not message item identity. This causes visible message loss in conversation history.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: False-positive merging of separate assistant messages in `resolveResponsesMessageSnapshotCollapse` when text is prefix-nested.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19, branch `fix/responses-message-collapse-106569`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ pnpm test packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  52 passed (52)

$ pnpm test src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  329 passed (329)
```

**Matrix-style evidence**:

| Input variant | Expected result | Verified |
|--------------|----------------|----------|
| Two message items, different `itemId`, prefix-nested text ("The answer" → "The answer is 42.") | Kept as 3 distinct text blocks | ✅ New test `keeps prefix-nested different-item messages as distinct blocks (#106569)` — `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` |
| Same message item (`msg_cumulative`), cumulative snapshots of progressively longer text | Collapsed into 1 final text block | ✅ Updated test `collapses same-item cumulative message snapshots into one text block (#91959)` — `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` |
| Same via transport stream (same `msg_cumulative` id with growing text) | Collapsed into 1 text block | ✅ `collapses cumulative message snapshot items into one text block (#91959)` — `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` (329 tests) |
| Same via completed-response backfill (same `msg_cumulative` id) | Collapsed into 1 text block | ✅ `collapses cumulative message snapshots in completed-response backfill (#91959)` — `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` |
| Non-prefix text, different items | Kept separate (unchanged) | ✅ Existing coverage |
| `itemId` undefined (backward compat) | Falls back to phase+prefix check | ✅ By design (optional field) |

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Different-item messages with prefix text remain separate (3 blocks with 3 different `textSignature`s and balanced lifecycle events)
2. Same-item cumulative snapshots still collapse correctly (1 final text block with lifecycle events matching prior text contents)
3. All 381 existing tests continue to pass (52 + 329)

**CI fix**: The initial PR run had 2 test failures in `checks-node-compact-large-1` — `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.base.test-utils.ts` had tests using `msg_1`/`msg_2`/`msg_3` (different itemIds) to simulate cumulative snapshots. After the itemId check, these were correctly kept separate. Fixed by using a single `msg_cumulative` id across all snapshots, matching real provider re-emission behavior.

**What was not tested**: Real-world OpenAI/Responses provider E2E — requires a provider that emits cumulative snapshots, which is not available in the local dev environment. The logic is fully covered by unit tests at the stream-processing level.

**Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
- ✅ Auth guard: No new paths — pure logic fix inside existing function. No policy/permission/feature flag needed.
- ✅ Enum completeness: All 3 call sites updated to pass `itemId`; optional field means `undefined` falls back to legacy behavior.
- ✅ Path coverage: Not a config change. All callers of `resolveResponsesMessageSnapshotCollapse` patched.
- ✅ Cleanup symmetry: `itemId` lives on `lastTextBlock` — lifecycle is naturally managed by the block lifecycle. No new state to clean up.
- ✅ Evidence match pattern: Logic/semantic bug → unit test matrix coverage (2 scenarios: different itemId → separate, same itemId → collapse).

## Root Cause

`resolveResponsesMessageSnapshotCollapse` (introduced in #92399) only compared `phase` and text prefix relation to decide whether to collapse. It did not check message item identity (`itemId`), so two semantically separate messages whose text happened to have a prefix relationship (e.g. a short message followed by a longer one starting with the same text) were incorrectly merged.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users of OpenAI-compatible Responses providers that send cumulative snapshots will no longer experience message loss when two separate assistant messages happen to have prefix-related text. Each message remains distinct in the conversation history.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — `itemId` is optional; undefined falls back to existing behavior.
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — adding `itemId` identity check is the minimal, correct guard. The collapse is conceptually "same-item cumulative snapshot replacement", so item identity is the right invariant.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the function's contract and interface are sound; this adds the missing dimension.
- **Alternative considered**: Removing snapshot collapse entirely — rejected because real providers do send cumulative snapshots (#91959), and without collapse the conversation would show repeated growing text blocks.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: iCodeMate <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: The fix was produced in an interactive session analyzing the bug in `resolveResponsesMessageSnapshotCollapse`. The AI suggested adding `itemId` as the identity check, and the human verified all three call sites and both test scenarios.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Providers that set `itemId` unreliably or inconsistently across snapshots of the same logical message.

**Mitigation**: The `itemId` check is gated on both `prior.itemId !== undefined` and `nextItemId !== undefined`. If either side lacks an `itemId`, the function falls back to the original phase+prefix behavior. This ensures compatibility with providers that don't emit item IDs, at the cost of retaining the original false-positive risk for those providers.

**Compatibility impact**: None for providers that don't emit itemId. For providers that do, message boundaries are now correctly preserved.

Fixes #106569

target.title: fix(context-engine): add symmetric readOnlyDiscovery->runtime lifecycle upgrade guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `registerContextEngineForOwner` blocks `readOnlyDiscovery→runtime` lifecycle upgrade unless callers know to pass `allowSameOwnerRefresh: true`. The guard structure is asymmetric: `runtime→readOnlyDiscovery` (re-discovery after live activation) has an explicit guard, but the reverse upgrade path is accidentally blocked by a generic re-registration check.

If triggered, the engine silently stays in `readOnlyDiscovery` mode and `resolveContextEngine` falls back to the default engine with a misleading warning: "until runtime activation registers it" — but runtime activation already ran and was silently rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing guard at `registerContextEngineForOwner` (registry.ts:555-558) explicitly allows `runtime→readOnlyDiscovery` (keep the runtime factory, skip registration), but the reverse `readOnlyDiscovery→runtime` upgrade falls through to the `allowSameOwnerRefresh` check (lines 560-562) which rejects the registration unless the caller opts in.

Currently latent because all plugin registration paths happen to pass `allowSameOwnerRefresh: true`, but this is coincidental — any new caller (third-party plugin, future code path) that omits this flag would hit the silent failure.

Fix: add an explicit symmetric guard before the `allowSameOwnerRefresh` check, matching the existing structure. This makes the intent self-documenting and the upgrade path robust regardless of `allowSameOwnerRefresh`.

## User Impact

None for current users — all existing plugin registration paths pass `allowSameOwnerRefresh: true`. Future plugin authors and new code paths are protected from silent lifecycle upgrade failures.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, `fix/bug-034-readonly-discovery-runtime-guard`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/context-engine/context-engine.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/context-engine/context-engine.test.ts

  RUN  v4.1.9 /media/vdb/code/github/openclaw

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  48 passed (48)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: All 48 context-engine tests pass. The new guard is a no-op for existing callers (they all pass `allowSameOwnerRefresh: true`, so the new `if` block is just a pass-through), and the existing test coverage for lifecycle transitions (`readOnlyDiscovery→runtime→readOnlyDiscovery` round-trip) continues to pass.

- **What was not tested**: No new test added for the standalone guard because existing test coverage already exercises the `readOnlyDiscovery→runtime` path via `allowSameOwnerRefresh: true`. The fix is structural: making the upgrade path explicit rather than coincidental.

### Real behavior proof

The guard change is a 4-line insert that mirrors the existing `runtime→readOnlyDiscovery` guard. Both transitions are now explicitly documented. The `allowSameOwnerRefresh` check's semantic is restored to its original purpose (allowing re-registration after module state resets) rather than accidentally guarding lifecycle upgrades.

### Open PR collision check

Searched open PRs touching `src/context-engine/registry.ts`: none found. Recent changes: #108179 (trim exports), #107315 (max-lines ratchet), #104668 (workboard fix). No overlapping fix.

---
