target.title: fix(doctor): pass collectModelsMap for agents.list model ref scan
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw doctor --fix` silently skips scanning legacy Codex model refs (`openai-codex/*`) in `agents.list.<id>.models.*` entries, causing incomplete migration warnings and potentially skipped repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

`collectConfigModelRefs` calls `collectAgentModelRefs` twice: once for `agents.defaults` (with `collectModelsMap: true`) and once for each `agents.list` entry (without `collectModelsMap`). The `collectModelsMap` parameter controls whether the agent's `models` map is scanned for legacy `openai-codex/*` model refs. The list-agent call was missing the parameter, making those entries invisible to the warning generator and the repair early-return gate.

The actual repair logic (`rewriteConfigModelRefsWithCompactionPolicy`) already handles list agents correctly. This fix only affects the detection/warning path, which also gates the early return in `maybeRepairCodexRoutes`.

## User Impact

Users with legacy Codex model refs only in `agents.list.<name>.models.<ref>` (not in `agents.defaults.models`) will now see accurate doctor warnings and have their config correctly repaired by `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## Evidence

- **One-line change**: add `collectModelsMap: true` to the `collectAgentModelRefs` call in the `agents.list` loop, matching the `agents.defaults` call on line 119.
- **Type check**: `pnpm tsgo:core` passes.
- **Formatting**: `oxfmt` passes.
- **No test regressions**: existing test suite continues to pass.

target.title: fix(media-understanding): add 3-level model fallback chain to video buildRequest
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where video understanding API requests could have an undefined `model` field when no explicit model is configured for the video entry. This caused silent API failures or unexpected provider-side default behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `runProviderEntry` function in `runner.entries.ts` has three capability branches — image, audio, and video. Both **image** (throws on missing model) and **audio** (3-level fallback chain) had model resolution. **Video** was the only branch that passed `entry.model` directly without any fallback.

The fix mirrors the proven audio pattern:
1. `entry.model?.trim()` — explicit model from entry config
2. `resolveDefaultMediaModel({ capability: "video" })` — provider manifest default or configured default
3. `entry.model` — last resort

`MediaUnderstandingCapability` already includes `"video"`, and `resolveDefaultMediaModel` already supports the video provider key (`provider.defaultModels?.["video"]`).

## User Impact

Users who configure video understanding without an explicit model will now get a reasonable default model instead of a `model: undefined` API call.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 24, branch `fix/bug-038-video-model-fallback`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/runner.video.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```console
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/runner.video.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: All 6 video runner tests pass. The fix is a 12-line additive change matching the existing audio pattern — no behavior change when `entry.model` is already set.
- **What was not tested**: No real third-party video API traffic tested. The fix relies on the same `resolveDefaultMediaModel` function already proven in the audio path.

### Real behavior proof

The existing test suite covers three scenarios:
- `preserves self-defaulting video providers without registry model metadata` — verifies that when the provider has no `defaultModels` and no entry model, the fallback chain correctly produces `undefined` (no regression)
- `does not use provider api config as video auth modelApi` — verifies auth resolution is unaffected
- The remaining 4 video tests cover normal model resolution, proxy fetch, and auth — all pass unchanged

### Collision check

Searched open PRs touching `runner.entries.ts` and merged PRs for "video model fallback" — no collision.

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Matrix polls had no outbound `pollMaxOptions` limit while the Matrix protocol (MSC3381) caps poll options at 20. Other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12) all declare their protocol limits.
- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and pass `maxOptions: 20` explicitly in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android pending-tool detail previews would show malformed Unicode when a tool argument's first line placed an emoji across the 160-code-unit truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending-tool detail previews truncate the first line at 157 UTF-16 code units before appending an ellipsis. That chokepoint now reuses the existing Android `takeUtf16Safe` helper (same helper already used for app session labels and notification text) so a split surrogate pair is dropped instead of rendered. The 160-code-unit size contract is unchanged.

To avoid inventing a new native i18n source template, truncation is bound to a local `preview` and rendered with the existing `$preview…` pattern. `native:i18n:sync` / locale artifacts / `android-app-i18n sync` remove the obsolete `${firstLine.take(157)}…` inventory entry and unused `native_09f0bda624faadd4` resources (net −1 inventory entry).

Collision check: searched open PRs for `ToolDisplay`, `takeUtf16Safe`, `preserve emoji` / UTF-16 Android tool preview; no competing open PR on this surface. Closest landed siblings: #108102 (session labels), #108101 / #108103 (Android UTF-16 status/reason paths).

## User Impact

- **Before:** an emoji landing on the 157-code-unit cut could leave a lone high surrogate in the pending-tool detail line.
- **After:** the preview stays well-formed Unicode; arguments that do not cross the limit render exactly as before.

## Verification

- Exact head: `68c5ed4f8c2762a0ddceb66d8016a494f8ea3eaa`
- `git diff --check` — passed
- `node --import tsx scripts/native-app-i18n.ts check` — passed (`changed=false`)

- Focused regression: `ToolDisplayRegistryTest.resolvePreservesUtf16BoundariesAtDetailPreviewLimit` (split + complete emoji at the 157-unit cut via `ToolDisplayRegistry.resolve` / `bash`+`command`)
- Hosted CI proof:
  - `android-test-play` PASS — https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29422003591/job/87374794646 (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, includes `ToolDisplayRegistryTest`)
  - `android-test-third-party` PASS — same workflow
  - `native-i18n` PASS — https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29422003591/job/87374794253

## Real behavior proof

### Production string operations (mirrors Kotlin String.take / Character.isHighSurrogate)

```bash
node --import tsx proof-android-tool-display-utf16.mts
```

```
node=v22.22.0
input.length=162 (156 prefix + 2-char emoji + 4-char 'tail')
input[156]=U+d83d (high surrogate)
input[157]=U+de00 (low surrogate)

=== Case 1: negative control (raw take) ===
  result.length=157
  result last code=U+d83d
  isHighSurrogate(last)=true
  ok: take(157) returns 157 code units
  ok: take(157) ends on a high surrogate (malformed Unicode)

=== Case 2: positive control (takeUtf16Safe) ===

  ok: takeUtf16Safe(157) returns ≤157 code units

=== Case 4: visual HTML proof ===
  html=/tmp/proof-tool-display-utf16.html

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed
```

### Visual rendering proof (headless Chrome, monospace matching Android FontFamily.Monospace)

The `proof-android-tool-display-utf16.mts` script renders the before/after text in a dark-themed monospace HTML page (mirroring the Android tool bubble styling) and captures it via `google-chrome --headless --screenshot`. The 800×520 PNG shows:

- **❌ BEFORE** (`String.take(157)`): text ends at a lone high surrogate U+D83D — Compose Text will render a tofu/box character
- **✅ AFTER split** (`takeUtf16Safe(157)`): emoji cleanly dropped at boundary, text is well-formed Unicode

- Asserts `detail == "<156 a's>…"` (no high surrogate at end)

target.title: fix(feishu): honor abortSignal in drive comment reply retry loop
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu's drive-comment reply lookup retries `FEISHU_COMMENT_REPLY_MISS_RETRY_LIMIT = 6` times with `FEISHU_COMMENT_REPLY_MISS_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 1_000` between attempts when the requested reply is not immediately visible in the embedded batch payload. The inter-attempt delay in `monitor.comment.ts:367` used `setTimeout(resolve, ms)` and never received the owning monitor account's `AbortSignal`. As a result, when `monitorSingleAccount` (line 469) tore down the websocket or webhook for an account restart, the in-flight comment retry loop ran through the full ~6 s poll-miss window instead of stopping with the rest of the account lifecycle.

`monitor.bot-identity.ts:40` in the same plugin already uses the shared `waitForAbortableDelay(ms, abortSignal)` helper for the bot-identity recovery retry; this missed the comment reply retry path. `monitor.comment.ts` exports the retry through `fetchDriveCommentContext` → `resolveDriveCommentEventTurn` → `handleFeishuCommentEvent` → `createFeishuDriveCommentNoticeHandler`; none of those four signatures accepted an `AbortSignal`, so the handler had no way to forward the account-level stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `delayMs` in `monitor.comment.ts` is now a thin wrapper over `waitForAbortableDelay` from `./async.js` and returns `Promise<boolean>` (true = full delay elapsed, false = aborted). The retry loop checks the returned boolean; a `false` (or a pre-aborted `abortSignal`) exits the loop on the next iteration rather than starting another 1 s delay.
- `fetchDriveCommentContext`, `ResolveDriveCommentEventParams`, `HandleFeishuCommentEventParams`, and `createFeishuDriveCommentNoticeHandler` each gain an optional `abortSignal?: AbortSignal` parameter.
- `monitorSingleAccount` already held `abortSignal` in scope (line 469) and is now the source — `registerEventHandlers` passes it through `createFeishuDriveCommentNoticeHandler({ ..., abortSignal })` so the handler can hand it to `handleFeishuCommentEvent`.
- No new config, no new env, no SDK change, no shared helper change. `waitForAbortableDelay` already handles the `{ once: true }` listener and the `timer.unref()` semantics correctly; the existing comment-handler retry case continues to mock `waitMs` and now provides the expected `Promise<boolean>` shape.

## User Impact

Stopping or restarting a Feishu account (ws disconnect, webhook stop, config reload) no longer leaves a drive-comment reply retry loop running for up to ~6 s after the rest of the account has settled. The reply-poll loop now exits on the next 1 s tick at most, which is the same cadence the sibling bot-identity recovery loop (`monitor.bot-identity.ts:40`) already follows. Reply-poll behavior on the happy path is unchanged — when the requested reply is found within the retry budget, the loop still breaks at the matching attempt.

## Collision / Differentiation Check

- #104431 (steipete, 2026-07-11, merged) refactored feishu and matrix retry loops onto `core retryAsync` and explicitly **skipped `feishu comment monitor`** with the rationale "result-predicate poll, not error retry". That refactor targets the error-retry contract (`retryAsync`); this PR targets the delay abort contract — the two are orthogonal.
- #106498 (hugenshen, 2026-07-14, merged) `fix(zalo): make poll error backoff abort-aware` — same pattern (poll/backoff loop honors `abortSignal`), different channel. The pattern this PR adopts is the one #106498 established for sibling plugin retry loops.
- #107454 (wahahaha1223, 2026-07-14, merged) `fix(usage): stop provider usage hangs after response headers` — same abort-on-outer-signal theme, different module.
- #108145 (ZengWen-DT, 2026-07-15, merged) `fix(clickclack): stop promptly during reconnect delay` — same theme of letting an outer lifecycle signal short-circuit an internal delay loop.
- A pre-submit `git log --since=2026-07-08 -- extensions/feishu/` search confirmed no merged or open PR touched `monitor.comment.ts`, `monitor.comment-notice-handler.ts`, `monitor.account.ts:344`, or `comment-handler.ts:52` in the same direction.

## Evidence

### Mutation proof — without the fix the new test fails

Patched to upstream `1f9a9281d9` (the rebased base) with only the test change applied (prod source stashed):

```text
 FAIL  |extension-feishu| extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment.test.ts > resolveDriveCommentEventTurn > stops the comment reply retry loop when the owning abortSignal fires
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 6 times

 ❯ extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment.test.ts:829:20

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 15 passed (17)
```

The pre-existing retry test also fails because the new `waitMs` signature requires `(ms, abortSignal?)`:

```text
AssertionError: expected 1st "vi.fn()" call to have been called with [ 1000, undefined ]
+ Received: [ 1000 ]
```

### After the fix — `extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment.test.ts`

```text
 RUN  v4.1.9 /tmp/feishu-fix

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
   Duration  11.45s (transform 6.95s, setup 119ms, import 10.81s, tests 217ms)
```

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.test.ts`:

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

### New regression test

`extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment.test.ts` adds one case (`stops the comment reply retry loop when the owning abortSignal fires`) that:

1. Spins up an `AbortController`, mounts it as `abortSignal` on `resolveDriveCommentEventTurn`, and gives `waitMs` a fixture that fires `abortController.abort()` on its first call.
2. Asserts `waitMs` is called exactly once (was 6 before the fix).
3. Asserts the second-argument position carries the controller's signal.
4. Asserts the replies endpoint is hit exactly once after the initial miss — no second, third, … retry fetch.
5. Asserts the requested reply stays unresolved (`targetReplyText === undefined`), confirming the loop exited without false-positive matching.

### Diff stat

```text
 extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.ts                 |  2 +
 extensions/feishu/src/monitor.account.ts                 |  1 +
 extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment-notice-handler.ts  |  4 +-

Prod-only non-test LOC is `+28 / -9` across four files.

### Static checks

```text
git diff --check: clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment-notice-handler.ts extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.account.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment.test.ts: pass (exit 0)
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json: pass (exit 0)
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 <5 changed files>: pass
```

### Focused non-i18n regression sweep

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/monitor.comment.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.startup.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.bot-menu.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.reaction.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.message-handler.test.ts

 Test Files  7 passed (7)
      Tests  82 passed (82)
   Duration  26.86s
```

The 17 failures observed in the full `extensions/feishu` sweep come from `extensions/feishu/src/setup-surface.test.ts` expecting English status strings ("Feishu: connected as …") while the test runtime has `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8` and the runtime emits the localized equivalent ("Feishu: 已连接为 …"). Reproducing the same 17 failures on a stock `1f9a9281d9` checkout (with this PR's changes stashed) confirms the failures predate this PR and are unrelated to the abort-propagation change.

## Not tested

- A live Feishu tenant with a real bot identity, real drive comment, and an account-restart signal firing mid-retry. The sanitized dev surface does not carry Feishu credentials, so the proof uses the same `resolveDriveCommentEventTurn` entry point with a mocked OpenAPI client and a synthetic abort — the contract change is observable end-to-end through `waitMs` call count and replies endpoint hit count, but the upstream Feishu server behavior is out of scope.
- `requestFeishuOpenApi` itself does not accept an `AbortSignal`; the comment-context HTTP calls already rely on `timeoutMs` for a bounded wait. This PR intentionally does not extend abort propagation into the HTTP fetch — that is a separate, larger refactor and would not be in scope for the poll-delay fix.
- The `delayMs` helper now returns `Promise<boolean>` (previously `Promise<void>`). The only caller inside `extensions/feishu/src/` is `resolveDriveCommentEventCore` via the default `waitMs = delayMs`; the test fixture `vi.fn(async () => {})` was updated to `vi.fn(async () => true)` so it explicitly signals "delay elapsed". Custom `waitMs` fixtures passed by any caller must now also return `boolean` to keep the retry loop running — this matches the contract of `waitForAbortableDelay` from `extensions/feishu/src/async.ts:68` and the pattern #106498 uses for zalo.

## Risk / Compatibility

- The retry-loop exit condition is now either `fetchedMatchedReply` found (unchanged) or `delayMs` returns false / `abortSignal?.aborted` (new). On the happy path the loop terminates on the same condition as before.
- `abortSignal` is optional on every signature; if no caller wires it through, `delayMs` falls back to `waitForAbortableDelay(ms, undefined)` which behaves identically to the old bare `setTimeout`. There is no behavior change for callers that never pass `abortSignal`.
- The only contract change for downstream test fixtures is `waitMs` returning `Promise<boolean>`; this is documented in the new test header comment.

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix(slack): add 30s timeout on read WebClients, not Bolt App.client
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Dedicated Slack **read** WebClients (`createSlackWebClient` / lookup) had no default Axios request timeout (except lookup’s existing 30s). Slow/hung Slack GETs could block indefinitely.

Bolt’s shared `App.client` must **not** inherit that deadline: mutations (reactions, chat.*, streaming) can be committed by Slack before the HTTP response returns; timing out then enables false failures and retries.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper P1 on earlier tips: putting `timeout ??= 30_000` on `resolveSlackWebClientOptions` also hits Bolt (`monitor/provider.ts` → `createSlackBoltApp({ clientOptions })`).

**Fix ownership:**
- `resolveSlackWebClientOptions` — shared/Bolt transport (proxy, retry defaults) — **no** default timeout
- `resolveSlackReadClientOptions` — read deadline (`SLACK_READ_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`)
- `createSlackWebClient` → read resolver
- lookup → same `SLACK_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`
- write / upload `timeout: 0` unchanged

## User Impact

- **Before:** Read clients could hang unbounded; earlier PR tip incorrectly risked timing out Bolt mutations.
- **After:** Probe/scopes/channel-style reads get a 30s default; Bolt `App.client` and write clients keep unbounded Axios unless explicitly configured.

## Evidence

### CI fix (1157dfb93bc7)

- `deadcode:exports`: `SLACK_READ_TIMEOUT_MS` is module-private; `resolveSlackReadClientOptions` stays in `client-options.ts` with production import from `client.ts` (no re-export).
- Tests assert ownership via `createSlackWebClient` / `createSlackLookupClient` + Bolt shared `timeout === undefined`.
- `oxfmt` applied to touched Slack client files. Unrelated `src/infra/file-read.ts` format noise (if still present) is outside this PR's diff.



**Head SHA:** `1157dfb93bc762b57cf546f137f3dcd6820cd59d`
**Base:** `55a822dc6877afd588dda6e8d17e64ba360041b5`

### L1 — owner-boundary unit tests (`client.test.ts`)

| Case | Expectation |
|---|---|
| `resolveSlackWebClientOptions()` (Bolt/shared) | `timeout` **undefined** |
| `resolveSlackReadClientOptions()` | `timeout === 30_000` |
| `createSlackWebClient(...)` | WebClient constructed with `timeout: 30_000` |
| explicit read override | preserved (`60_000`) |
| write defaults / `timeout: 0` | no default timeout; `0` preserved |
| `createSlackLookupClient(...)` | `timeout: 30_000` + `rejectRateLimitedCalls` |

### Call-chain proof (source)

- Bolt: `extensions/slack/src/monitor/provider.ts` uses `resolveSlackWebClientOptions()` only
- Reads: `createSlackWebClient` → `resolveSlackReadClientOptions`

### Rank-up vs prior tip

Removed shared-client timeout; added dedicated read resolver + Bolt/shared regression coverage. L3 redacted live proof below covers real API reads and slow-endpoint ownership for Bolt/shared vs read deadline.

### L3 — live Slack API + slow-endpoint ownership (redacted)

Exact head: `d23b89d39f1385b9f5f1ae5612f99a54f5d61719`

Tokens were supplied via local env for this run only; **not** written to the PR, repo, or logs below.

```text

Host: zwdeMacBook-Pro.local
Time: 2026-07-15T23:16:25.571Z

=== Option ownership (final tip contracts) ===
Bolt/shared resolveSlackWebClientOptions().timeout: undefined
Read resolveSlackReadClientOptions().timeout: 30000
Write resolveSlackWriteClientOptions().timeout: undefined

=== Real Slack API (auth.test + bounded read) ===
✓ read client (bot, timeout=30s): ok=true user=U0***1V team=T0***2Z elapsed_ms=680
✓ Bolt/shared client (bot, no default timeout): ok=true user=U0***1V team=T0***2Z elapsed_ms=381
✓ write client (bot, no default timeout): ok=true user=U0***1V team=T0***2Z elapsed_ms=339
✓ read client (user token, timeout=30s): ok=true user=U0***7C team=T0***2Z elapsed_ms=310
✓ users.list limit=1 via read client: ok=true members=1 elapsed_ms=376

=== Controlled slow endpoint (deadline vs Bolt/shared) ===
[WARN]  web-api:WebClient:5 http request failed timeout of 30000ms exceeded
Read client against 32s delay (timeout=30s): timed out/rejected at 30009ms: A request error occurred: timeout of 30000ms exceeded

## What Problem This Solves

Current CI `check-test-types` fails in `extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/monitor.replay.test.ts` because the mock `ServerResponse.writeHead()` mutates `this.headersSent`, and strict test type checking infers `this` as `{}` for that object-literal method.

## Evidence

Closes #108526

AI-assisted: yes

## What Problem This Solves

Fresh `2026.7.2-beta.1` installs can complete ChatGPT OAuth and the live inference probe, then fail before the verified credential is saved:

Runtime normalization can materialize `auth.profiles` while the authored config omits `auth`. Manual-auth activation used the normalized config as its conflict baseline, then compared it with the authored source at commit time. The shape difference was reported as a provider edit.

This change keeps separate runtime and authored-source baselines. The live probe still rejects provider changes against the latest runtime config. The config commit also rejects edits against the original authored source. Applying the verified patch no longer compares a normalized object shell with a source-only omission.

Fresh installs can finish ChatGPT OAuth when runtime defaults add empty config containers. Provider or model changes made during the live probe still stop credential persistence.

target.title: fix(memory): bound unsignaled remote HTTP with default timeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory remote HTTP (`withRemoteHttpResponse`) only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Embedding batch / `postJson` callers often omit a signal (Google/OpenAI/Voyage upload and status polls), so a peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could hang the Gateway forever. Idle body caps never start until headers arrive. Callers that pass a cancellation-only `AbortSignal` (no deadline) had the same hang risk when the wrapper treated any signal as a reason to skip the transport floor.

Hosted OpenAI/Voyage/Google callers also needed a tighter 120s floor than local/self-hosted Ollama/LM Studio (600s), without exporting timeout-policy constants on the public plugin SDK.

## Why This Change Was Made

Install a shared hang floor via existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs`, and compose it with any caller `AbortSignal`:

- Default local/self-hosted floor: 600s (`withRemoteHttpResponse`)
- Hosted/cloud floor: 120s via `withHostedRemoteHttpResponse`, `fetchHostedRemoteEmbeddingVectors`, and `createHostedRemoteEmbeddingProvider`
- Explicit `timeoutMs` override still wins
- Timeout constants stay package-private (not public plugin SDK exports)

Wire hosted providers (OpenAI, Voyage, Google, GitHub Copilot, DeepInfra, Mistral, shared batch upload) to the hosted helpers. Keep LM Studio on the local `createRemoteEmbeddingProvider` path.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled (or cancellation-only-signaled) memory remote HTTP could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream. Hosted providers inherited a 10-minute floor.

**After:** Local/self-hosted requests fail closed after 600s by default; hosted provider paths fail closed after 120s. Explicit `timeoutMs` and earlier caller aborts still win.

## Evidence

- Changed: `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.ts`, `post-json.ts`, `embeddings-remote-fetch.ts`, `embeddings-remote-provider.ts`, `batch-upload.ts`, hosted provider callers, plugin SDK barrel (no timeout-constant exports), surface budget pins
- Production path under test: OpenAI/Voyage `fetchHostedRemoteEmbeddingVectors` → `postJson` → `withRemoteHttpResponse` against a real local `node:http` server that never writes headers
- Regression: remote-http, embeddings-remote-fetch, post-json, batch-upload, openai/google/voyage provider+batch tests; `plugin-sdk-surface-report --check`

## Real behavior proof

### Caller path

`extensions/openai/embedding-provider.ts` / `extensions/voyage/embedding-provider.ts` → `fetchHostedRemoteEmbeddingVectors` → `postJson` → guarded fetch hang floor (120s default; 80ms override in hung-server fixture).

Google/Copilot/batch upload → `withHostedRemoteHttpResponse` (120s default).

DeepInfra/Mistral → `createHostedRemoteEmbeddingProvider` (120s default).

LM Studio remains on `createRemoteEmbeddingProvider` (600s local default).

### Commands

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.test.ts \
  packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-remote-fetch.test.ts \

node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check
```

### Evidence after fix

Fixes an issue where terminal users setting up a channel could not revise an earlier answer or return from the selected channel's first prompt to the channel picker. target.title: fix(agents): gate compaction rotation for sqlite-backed sessions
target.body:
Closes #104769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents using sqlite-backed session storage could hit an
`ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir 'sqlite:...'` error path when
compaction transcript rotation ran through the post-flip `run/attempt.ts` call
site. Rotation tries to compute a successor transcript path with
`path.dirname(sessionFile)`, but for sqlite-backed sessions `sessionFile` is a
`sqlite:<agentId>:<sessionId>:<storePath>` marker string, not a filesystem
path, so the derived "directory" is nonsense.

## Why This Change Was Made

`compact.ts` already guards its own rotation call with
`!isSqliteSessionTranscript`, but `run/attempt.ts`'s call site (added after
compaction call sites were split) did not carry the same guard, so
sqlite-backed sessions rotated through that path still hit the bug. Rather
than duplicating the guard at each call site, this moves the check inside
`rotateTranscriptAfterCompaction()` itself (using the existing
`parseSqliteSessionFileMarker` helper), so every current and future caller is
protected by construction.

## User Impact

Agents configured with `truncateAfterCompaction: true` and sqlite-backed
session storage no longer risk a rotation failure/error noise after
compaction; sqlite-backed sessions now cleanly skip rotation instead of
attempting an invalid filesystem write.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test asserting `rotateTranscriptAfterCompaction()`
  returns `{ rotated: false, reason: "sqlite-backed session" }` for a
  `sqlite:...` session file marker.
- Proved the regression: temporarily removed the new guard and reran the test,
  which failed with
  `ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir 'C:\...\sqlite:test-agent:test-session:...'`
  — matching the exact failure mode described in the issue. Restored the fix
  and confirmed the test passes again.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-successor-transcript.test.ts` — 13/13 passed.
- This PR is agent-assisted (GitHub Copilot CLI); tested locally per the evidence above, CI will run full type/lint/test gates on push.

target.title: fix: clarify SQLite version error message to prevent user confusion
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users seeing the SQLite version error would be confused by the message "3.44.6+" and think it meant "3.44.6 and above", when in fact only the 3.44.x series received the WAL-reset bug fix. This led to confusion when versions like 3.46.1 were rejected despite being numerically higher than 3.44.6.

The issue was reported in #108273 where a user with Node 24.18.0 (SQLite 3.46.1) thought their version should be accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The error message has been clarified to explicitly state "3.44.6+ in the 3.44.x series" and "3.50.7+ in the 3.50.x series" instead of just "3.44.6+ or 3.50.7+". This matches the SQLite team's actual fix announcement which only backported the WAL-reset bug fix to specific minor version series (3.44.x and 3.50.x), plus the main fix in 3.51.3+.

The code logic remains unchanged - this is purely a clarity improvement to the error message.

## User Impact

Users who encounter the SQLite version check error will now immediately understand why their version is not accepted, without needing to research SQLite version numbering or the WAL-reset bug fix history. The message now clearly explains that only specific version series received the fix.

## Evidence

- All existing tests pass: 22 tests in `src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts`
- Build succeeds: `pnpm build` completed successfully
- Type checking passes: `pnpm tsgo:core` has no errors
- The error message now explicitly states which version series are safe:
  - "3.44.6+ in the 3.44.x series"

## What Problem This Solves

Slack provider startup could wait indefinitely when the boot-time `auth.test` HTTP request stalled before returning headers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup identity validation now uses a dedicated Slack WebClient with a 10-second transport timeout, zero retries, and immediate rate-limit rejection. It preserves the resolved `SLACK_API_URL` and proxy agent, while leaving Bolt's long-lived listener client and its transport policy unchanged.

When the bounded request fails, startup follows the existing degraded path and retains the required-mention fail-closed warning.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

A stalled Slack identity check terminates after about 10 seconds instead of blocking startup indefinitely. Slack then continues through the existing degraded startup behavior.

## Evidence

The reviewer explicitly checked coexistence with the newly landed Slack identity-health/degraded-status behavior.
- Previous-head CI isolated one test-only logger mock variance error; the exact head now implements the runtime contract as `(...args: unknown[]) => void` and safely narrows the first argument before inspecting the message.
- GitHub CI for the refreshed exact head passed [run `29459929560`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29459929560) with 35 successful jobs, 0 failures, 0 pending jobs, and `openclaw/ci-gate` green.

The committed regression test uses the real startup-scoped `@slack/web-api` WebClient against a loopback `node:http` server configured through `SLACK_API_URL`. The server accepts the request and deliberately never returns response headers.

web-api warning: http request failed timeout of 10000ms exceeded
stalled transport test duration: 10078ms
socket close: observed before server cleanup
startup order: auth-settled before app-start

A companion client test proves that the startup policy preserves the supplied proxy agent and Slack API root while forcing `timeout: 10000`, `retries: 0`, and `rejectRateLimitedCalls: true`.

target.title: fix(ai): normalize non-conforming tool-call ids reaching Anthropic/Google targets (#95623)
target.body:
Fixes #95623

## What Problem This Solves

After a cross-provider failover, an OpenAI-responses composite tool-call id (`call_XXX|fc_YYY`) can reach an **Anthropic** target still containing the `|`. Anthropic requires tool ids matching `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, so it hard-400s the whole replay and the session is bricked for its own primary provider — no new turns without a reset.

This happens on two paths that the existing `#61254` sanitizer misses:
- **Orphaned tool result** — the paired tool call was dropped (compaction/windowing), so there is no in-pass map entry and the raw id passes through untouched.
- **Same-model-tagged call** — a failover-introduced id whose provenance looks same-model as the Anthropic target skips normalization (`!isSameModel` guard), so both the call and its result keep the `|`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`packages/ai/src/providers/transform-messages.ts` owns cross-provider tool-call-id normalization but only normalized `toolCall` ids when `!isSameModel`, and `toolResult` ids only via an in-pass `toolCallIdMap`. Non-conforming ids leaked through both gaps.

A blanket "always normalize" is unsafe: the OpenAI-completions/OpenAI-responses/Mistral normalizers are **not idempotent** on their own native ids (openai-completions strips the `|fc_…` half; openai-responses reads the `source` message; mistral is a stateful id map), so applying them to same-model native ids would corrupt valid replays.

So `transformMessages` gains an opt-in `targetSafeToolCallIds` flag, passed `true` only by the **Anthropic and Google** call sites whose normalizers are charset scrubs that are idempotent on their native ids. In target-safe mode every tool id reaching the target is normalized — the same-model call and the map-miss result included — and because the scrub is deterministic, a call and its result stay paired. Every other provider keeps the default (`false`), so their behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

The shared transform owns this invariant, so the fix stays there (not at the Anthropic transport-serialization boundary, which cannot see the shared call/result pairing). Non-goals: no change to any provider's normalizer semantics, no change to cross-provider behavior, and no id-collision hashing.

## User Impact

Sessions that fail over to an OpenAI-responses model and later replay to an Anthropic primary no longer brick on an Anthropic 400 — the foreign composite id is scrubbed to a conforming id (`call_XXX_fc_YYY`) on both the call and its result. Google targets get the same protection. OpenAI/Mistral users are unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior via the actual `transformMessages` (Anthropic target, composite id `call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01`), head `e7e315d6c5a3`:

~~~text
AFTER S1-safe orphan (targetSafe=true):          ["result:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01"]                                | PIPE-SURVIVES=false
AFTER S3-safe same-model-mistag (targetSafe=true): ["call:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01","result:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01"] | PIPE-SURVIVES=false
REGRESSION default (targetSafe=false) same-model:  ["call:call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01","result:call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01"] | PIPE-SURVIVES=true
~~~

The two target-safe paths scrub the `|`; the default path leaves a same-model id byte-for-byte untouched (proving no OpenAI/Mistral corruption). On current `main` (target-safe absent) both S1 and S3 leak — `PIPE-SURVIVES=true`.

- `vitest run packages/ai/src/providers/transform-messages.test.ts` — 5 passed (2 red-first #95623 guards for S1/S3 + 3 regressions: default-mode composite untouched, cross-provider pair still mapped, source-requiring normalizer never invoked on a map-miss result).
- Negative control: with the source fix stashed, the S1 & S3 guard tests fail (`expected 'call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01' to be 'call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01'`) — confirms the tests guard the bug.
- Broader regression: all `packages/ai/src/providers` tests — 356 passed; the 1 failure (`openai-chatgpt-responses` zstd-SSE encoding) reproduces identically with my change stashed, i.e. pre-existing/unrelated (a zstd env issue on this host).
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` / `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` — no errors; `oxfmt --check` — clean; `check:loc` — passes (all growth in the sub-500-line transform; the three oversized provider files stay net-zero).

## Notes

- Distinct from #95671 (guarded only the same-model path at the transport-serialization boundary, missing orphan results) and #95629 — this fixes both leak paths at the owning transform boundary with zero cross-provider regression.
- AI-assisted (Claude Code); I have reviewed and understand every line.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Some deployments serve a Claude/MiniMax model through a proxy that intermittently degrades a native `tool_use` block into plain text. In that degraded case the tool call arrives as the namespaced/bare XML attribute dialect — `<invoke name="tool"><parameter name="x">v</parameter></invoke>`, optionally wrapped in `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` and optionally prefixed with `antml:` or `mm:`.

On current `main` two gaps remained:

1. The visible-text sanitizer recognized the `antml:` prefix but not the `mm:` prefix, so a degraded `mm:invoke` block leaked verbatim into the user-visible reply.
2. The persist-path stripper (`packages/tool-call-repair` `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) did not recognize the attribute-dialect invoke at all, so an unfenced standalone degraded invoke block was written into the durable `done.message` instead of being scrubbed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user, and it must not be persisted into session state either — but a legitimate code example of the same markup (inside a fenced or inline code span) must be preserved, not deleted. This change teaches both layers about the full attribute dialect using a closed `(?:antml:|mm:)?` namespace allow-list, so arbitrary `ns:` tokens in prose are never matched.

This PR was re-implemented on top of current `main` after upstream refactored the tool-call-repair package (the new `scanXmlishToolCall` seam and code-region helpers). The change is scoped to the net delta that still reproduces on `main`:

- **Visible text** (`assistant-visible-text.ts`): mirror the existing `antml:` handling for the `mm:` namespace in the tag-name scan, quick-check, and payload-start patterns. The `<function_calls>`-wrapped bare-invoke case is already scrubbed by the package strip stage in the delivery pipeline.
- **Persist path** (`packages/tool-call-repair`): a dedicated linear scanner recognizes a complete standalone invoke block (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `<function_calls>` wrapper, self-closing, and zero-parameter forms). The scanner returns `none`/`incomplete`/`complete`, so on an unterminated open the strip loop bails and preserves the remainder — exactly mirroring the existing dialects — keeping the scan linear on adversarial input.
- **Code-region awareness**: the strip takes an optional code-region predicate evaluated at the block's start offset. Fenced/inline Markdown examples of the invoke dialect are preserved while unfenced standalone leaked blocks are scrubbed. Without a predicate the package strip lazily computes code regions so a bare call still spares examples.
- **Plugin SDK contract preserved**: the exported `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it forces a scrub of every region, even inside code, for untrusted callers), with code-aware behavior available only via the explicit `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` opt-in.
- **Layering**: `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode`/`CodeRegion` were moved into `normalization-core` (the package's only dependency) so `tool-call-repair` can share one implementation without importing app source; `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` re-exports them so existing callers are unaffected.

Non-goals/boundaries: the native Anthropic/DSML transports are untouched; no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced; the equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged; the invoke dialect is recognized only by the strip/sanitize paths (never promoted to an executable call and never wired into the stream-buffering scanner).

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude/MiniMax routes no longer see raw namespaced/bare `invoke` tool-call XML in their replies, and the leaked block is no longer written into the persisted message (no session-state content loss). Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped. A resolved-review audit also removed an O(n²) worst case on the persist strip path, so adversarial degraded text cannot cause pathological CPU use.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests were added at the layers that own the contract:
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: invoke-dialect variants (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `function_calls` wrapper, self-closing, zero-param), code-region preservation vs. unfenced scrub, the predicate override, and a linear-time guard against many unterminated opens.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts`: the `preserveCodeRegions` opt-in and strict default.
- `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts`: the `mm:invoke`/`mm:parameter` visible-text case (parallel to the existing `antml:` case), alongside existing standalone-vs-inline `function_calls` delivery-path coverage.

Real-behavior proof (before = current `main`, after = this branch), driving the actual `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` and `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` on the leak shapes:

```
=== BEFORE (main) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it.\n<mm:invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<mm:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</mm:parameter>\n</mm:invoke>"
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>"
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (preserved)

=== AFTER (this branch) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it."
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done."
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (still preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (still preserved)
```

The three real leak shapes (A2 visible `mm:`, A3 visible `function_calls`-wrapped bare invoke, C1 persisted unfenced standalone invoke) are now scrubbed, while the fenced (B1) and inline (B2) code examples remain untouched — the exact over-scrub concern is verified closed.

O(n²) audit fix: a resolved-review pass measured the persist strip degrading quadratically on adversarial input with many unterminated invoke opens (720 KB ≈ 977 ms, scaling to seconds for a few MB). Making the scanner bail on `incomplete` (mirroring the existing unterminated-candidate bail) brought the same 720 KB input to ≈ 0.8 ms and restored linear scaling; a regression test locks this.

Verification: `tool-call-repair` grammar/payload/stream-normalizer (157 passed), `provider-stream-shared` + `tool-payload` + `assistant-visible-text` + `sanitize-text` + `message-action-runner.send-validation` + `embedded-agent-utils` (all green), `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` exit 0 (surface budget bumped by the one new `StripPlainTextToolCallOptions` type), oxfmt clean, `git diff --check` clean. Rebased onto current `main` (`9b823c61`).

target.title: fix(android): preserve emoji in tool detail previews
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android pending-tool detail previews would show malformed Unicode when a tool argument's first line placed an emoji across the 160-code-unit truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending-tool detail previews truncate the first line at 157 UTF-16 code units before appending an ellipsis. That chokepoint now reuses the existing Android `takeUtf16Safe` helper (same helper already used for app session labels and notification text) so a split surrogate pair is dropped instead of rendered. The 160-code-unit size contract is unchanged.

To avoid inventing a new native i18n source template, truncation is bound to a local `preview` and rendered with the existing `$preview…` pattern. `native:i18n:sync` / locale artifacts / `android-app-i18n sync` remove the obsolete `${firstLine.take(157)}…` inventory entry and unused `native_09f0bda624faadd4` resources (net −1 inventory entry).

Collision check: searched open PRs for `ToolDisplay`, `takeUtf16Safe`, `preserve emoji` / UTF-16 Android tool preview; no competing open PR on this surface. Closest landed siblings: #108102 (session labels), #108101 / #108103 (Android UTF-16 status/reason paths).

## User Impact

- **Before:** an emoji landing on the 157-code-unit cut could leave a lone high surrogate in the pending-tool detail line.
- **After:** the preview stays well-formed Unicode; arguments that do not cross the limit render exactly as before.

## Verification

- Exact head: `68c5ed4f8c2762a0ddceb66d8016a494f8ea3eaa`
- `git diff --check` — passed

  - `android-test-play` PASS — https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29422003591/job/87374794646 (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, includes `ToolDisplayRegistryTest`)
  - `android-test-third-party` PASS — same workflow
  - `native-i18n` PASS — https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29422003591/job/87374794253

## Real behavior proof

### Production string operations (mirrors Kotlin String.take / Character.isHighSurrogate)

```bash

```

```

=== Case 1: negative control (raw take) ===

### Visual rendering proof (headless Chrome, monospace matching Android FontFamily.Monospace)

The `proof-android-tool-display-utf16.mts` script renders the before/after text in a dark-themed monospace HTML page (mirroring the Android tool bubble styling) and captures it via `google-chrome --headless --screenshot`. The 800×520 PNG shows:

## What Problem This Solves

`findCursorInteractiveElements` truncates DOM text inside a **browser** `Runtime.evaluate` page expression with `.slice(0, 101)`. At an emoji/surrogate boundary that cut can leave a **lone high surrogate** on the CDP `returnByValue` wire. Node `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 100)` is a **no-op** when the string is already `length === 100`, so the malformed unit survives. Approaches that *call* Node/SDK `truncateUtf16Safe` **inside** the page expression throw `ReferenceError` and fail closed to an empty cursor map.

## Why This Change Was Made

Own the cut in a **page-local**, dependency-free helper injected via `Function#toString`, with a unified page/Node preview budget of **100**.

**Stronger than [#108316](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108316):** that helper only rewinds when the cut splits a live surrogate pair (`end < length` and next is low). This tip also **scrubs a trailing high surrogate when `length === max` already holds a lone unit** (the exact residue unsafe `.slice` leaves and Node cannot repair). Helper lives in `cdp-page-text-preview.ts` imported by `cdp.ts` so Knip/`deadcode:exports` sees a production consumer (fixes the unused-export CI failure from exporting off `cdp.ts`).

Non-goals: no live Chrome CDP redesign; do not inject `truncateUtf16Safe.toString()` alone.

## User Impact

- **Before:** Unsafe page `.slice` can put a lone surrogate on the evaluate payload; Node re-truncate at the final budget may leave it. Node-helper-in-page calls empty the cursor-interactive map.
- **After:** Page preview truncate is UTF-16 safe before `returnByValue`, including length===max residues; Node re-cap stays defense-in-depth.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `db1577aaf6436e03a96013ce869bb135cda9be7d`
**Base:** `8e6f966482b0fb2253498fb468cae840382f337b`

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Full-string cut at emoji / 100 budget | drops whole emoji; no lone surrogate |
| **Residue repair:** unsafe `.slice(0,100)` then page helper | scrub lone high; 108316-style split-only cut leaves it |
| Node `truncateUtf16Safe(unsafe, 100)` | still lone (documents the hole) |
| Injected expression via `Function#toString` | embeds page helper; does **not** call `truncateUtf16Safe(` |
| `deadcode:exports` | helper exported from its module with `cdp.ts` production import |

Focused tests: `extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-page-text-preview.test.ts`（含 main 旧管道的回归测试）。

## Review

- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

### Chrome CDP 实时输出（复审要求）

连接 Chrome/138.0.7204.157 headless（V8 13.8.258.26），通过 WebSocket 执行 `Runtime.evaluate` + `returnByValue: true`，验证 `truncateCdpPageTextPreview` 注入后的光标预览结果。

**实验 1：main 当前 `.slice(0, 101)` 管道在 CDP 线上产生孤立代理项 ← 缺陷复现**

输入 `"a".repeat(100) + "😀"`（102 UTF-16 单元）。😀（U+1F600 = `😀`）从位置 100 开始。`.slice(0, 101)` 捕获位置 100 的高代理位 0xD83D，但不含位置 101 的低代理位。

```
CDP Runtime.evaluate 返回:
{
  "inputLength": 102,
  "pageSliceLength": 101,
  "lastCharCodeHex": "0xD83D",
  "hasLoneSurrogate": true,
  "note": "🔴 lone surrogate enters CDP returnByValue"
}
```

> 🔴 孤立高代理位通过 `returnByValue` 进入 CDP 序列化。Node 端 `truncateUtf16Safe(_, 100)` 后续截断可弃掉该位，但线上已传输了残缺单元。

**实验 2：`truncateCdpPageTextPreview(100)` 修复后无孤立代理项**

相同输入 → 页面级 `truncateCdpPageTextPreview(text, 100)`

```
{
  "inputLength": 102,
  "resultLength": 100,
  "resultContent": "a×100",
  "hasLoneSurrogate": false,
  "verified": "PASS ✓"
}
```

> ✅ 页面级截断在 `returnByValue` 前完成，输出无孤立代理项。

**实验 3：真实 DOM 文本 205 单元：旧管道与新管道对比**

创建含有 40 个 🚀 的 DOM 元素（205 UTF-16 单元），分别执行 main 的 `.slice(0,101)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(100)` 和新管道。

```
{
  "rawLength": 205,
  "old.page.slice(0,101)": "101 units",
  "old.hasLoneSurrogate (before Node)": false,
  "Node truncateUtf16Safe(_,100) result": "99 units (band-aid on 101)",
  "new.preview (truncateCdpPageTextPreview)": "99 units",
  "new.hasLoneSurrogate": false
}
```

> ✅ 不同内容布局下，新管道始终无孤立代理项。

**实验 4：`Function#toString` 注入至浏览器页面**

通过 `${fn.toString()}` 嵌入到 `Runtime.evaluate` 表达式，在页面作用域执行。

```

  "hasTruncateUtf16SafeRef": "NO ✓",
  "roundTripOk": "YES ✓",
  "testText": "121-unit string with 30 emoji + text",
  "truncatedLength": 100,
  "hasLoneSurrogate": "NO ✓",
  "verdict": "PASS"
}
```

> ✅ 函数体不引用 `truncateUtf16Safe`（无 ReferenceError），注入后可在页面作用域正常执行。

target.title: fix: queued voice replies are lost when the delivery queue retries them
target.body:
Closes #108501

**Prompt request:** Keep a queued voice reply deliverable after the producer's temporary media is cleaned up and the producer dies, without widening what a send is allowed to read.

**Proof target:** A fresh process recovers byte-identical audio for a queued voice reply whose original temp no longer exists, while immediate sends stay copy-free and live-only media is never persisted.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with automatic TTS would silently lose voice replies whenever the outbound delivery queue retried them.

Automatic TTS synthesizes into a temporary file owned by the producing process, and the raw path of that file is stored in the durable delivery queue. The file is removed when the producer exits, and unconditionally five minutes after synthesis. The queue's own retry budget is roughly 22.5 minutes, so the cleanup lands inside it: later retries read a path that no longer exists. Recovery also commonly runs in a different process than the one that enqueued the entry, and that process never had the temp at all.

The message was already accepted into the write-ahead queue, so the system had effectively promised to deliver it. Instead the reply is dropped. The resulting `Local media file not found` is not classified as a permanent error, so the entry consumes all five retries before being dead-lettered, and the text of the reply is lost along with the audio.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queue now owns the media it promises to replay. Before a deliverable row is published, each authorized local source is read through the same media access the live send already uses and copied into a queue-owned artifact directory; only the queue payload is rewritten to point at that copy. The live send keeps the original path and stays copy-free, so immediate delivery is unchanged.

Staging resolves the media read capability exactly as the live send resolves it, so it can neither reject media the send would deliver nor read more than the send may; both paths now share one resolver instead of keeping separate argument lists.

Ownership is proven by process identity rather than by a marker file, a lease table, or a clock. Artifacts are grouped per producing process generation (`<pid>-<processStartTime>-<nonce>`), and a generation is reclaimed only when its owner is provably gone. A live owner, an owner whose identity cannot be verified, and a recycled PID whose start time no longer matches are each handled without deleting media that a pending row still needs. Wall-clock age is never an ownership signal, so a gateway that has been idle for a long time keeps its own undelivered media.

Ordering is durable-state-first: the row transition commits before any artifact is unlinked, so a crash in between leaves a reclaimable orphan rather than a row whose media is gone. The retain set is re-read after each death proof, because a short-lived producer can commit a row and exit while a sweep is already running; this is sufficient rather than merely narrower, since a process only ever stages into its own generation.

Scope is deliberately narrow: no database schema change, no new status value, no new configuration surface, no public SDK export, and no lease or owner table. Cross-platform owner identity reuses the existing readers — `getFileLockProcessStartTime` on POSIX and `readWindowsProcessStartTimeSync` on Windows — behind one helper, replacing a pairing that `gateway-lock.ts` had previously kept private.

Sensitive media is treated as live-only throughout: it reaches neither the artifact directory nor the row, so a `required` send fails closed before dispatch and a `best_effort` send degrades to live-only rather than persisting a row it cannot replay.

## User Impact

Voice replies that are deferred or retried now actually arrive. Previously they were dropped silently, together with their accompanying text, after burning the full retry budget.

There is one deliberate trade-off. When a local media source cannot be staged — unreadable, unauthorized, or oversized — a `best_effort` send now creates no durable row and is delivered live-only, and a `required` send fails closed before any platform dispatch. Previously both persisted a row referencing the raw source path. That row was never actually replayable: recovery resolves media through the same loader and access policy as the live send, so a source the queue cannot read is one the retry cannot read either, and the old behavior spent all five retries before dead-lettering while also losing the text. The cost is that a transient filesystem error on an otherwise-good file now drops write-ahead protection for that one send. That is preferable to persisting a raw producer-owned path as a fallback, which is exactly the unreplayable row this change exists to eliminate.

## Evidence

Verified on `2026.7.2`, Node 24.15.0, Linux.

**Observable before/after.** Real OpenRouter Kokoro TTS produced a voice payload; the durable row was committed; the producer then parked with a live event loop so OpenClaw's real 5-minute temp cleanup could fire, and was killed with `SIGKILL` (not a clean exit, which would run cleanup hooks a real crash never runs). A genuinely fresh process then replayed the entry through the production Telegram reconnect drain (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/delivery-queue-runtime` → `drainPendingDeliveries`, with no injected delivery implementation, so the runtime lazy-loads the real internal deliver).

Both sides ran the same harness against the same source bytes, with OpenClaw's real 5-minute cleanup observed firing at ~300.2 s in each:

| | before (clean `main`) | after (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| producer temp after cleanup | deleted | deleted |
| producer death | `SIGKILL` | `SIGKILL` |
| fresh-process drain | fails: `file not found \| not-found` | reaches the adapter's `sendVoice` |
| queue-owned copy | none | byte-identical to the source (SHA-256 match) |

Before the change the entry cannot even reach the transport, because resolving the media fails first. After it, the recovered bytes match the original by SHA-256 and size, and the entry reaches the real adapter's outbound request. An earlier run of the same after-fix sequence with a live OpenRouter Kokoro synthesis produced the same result on real provider audio.

**Tests.** The changed-surface suites pass. One case places its media in an agent workspace that is reachable only through the agent-scoped capability — root expansion is disabled and the state directory sits outside the media roots, so nothing else can admit it. That case fails if staging reverts to the raw media access, if the shared resolver is bypassed, or if the agent identity is dropped from it. Also included is a real child-process crash integration test that commits the row, `SIGKILL`s the producer, and proves a fresh process retains the artifact its pending row needs, reads identical bytes after the producer's source is deleted, and drops the artifact once the row is acked.

The safety-critical assertions are mutation-tested: inverting generation ownership, forcing PID-reuse to look alive, removing the atomic rename, removing partial-stage cleanup, disabling the sensitive-media gate, and snapshotting the GC retain set each fail the suite.

**Static gates.** `tsgo` (core and tests), oxlint, oxfmt, `pnpm build` (0 ineffective dynamic imports), 0 import cycles, the database-first legacy-store guard, and the plugin SDK surface check all pass.

**Scope.** 23 files, +1508/-53; production +551/-51, tests +957/-2. One topic: queued outbound media ownership.

**Limitations.**

- Reclamation runs only when ownership is proven dead. A generation is reclaimed when its owner is provably gone or when a live PID's start time no longer matches; a live owner and an owner whose identity cannot be verified are both retained. Retention is therefore conservative by design, and this change does not make on-disk spool storage strictly bounded. An unverifiable owner keeps its generation until ownership can be proven, which is most likely on platforms where process start time depends on external tooling. This is a deliberate bias: retaining an artifact costs disk, while reclaiming one that a pending row still needs costs the user's message. A size quota is intentionally not part of this change, since fail-closed admission would introduce a separate path that drops durability.
- Reclamation runs from gateway maintenance, which matches the lifecycle of the queue it serves: every drain and recovery caller is gateway-hosted, so without a gateway a pending row is never replayed either and its media is still required rather than reclaimable.
- End-to-end user receipt of the recovered voice is not claimed here. The proof stops at the real adapter's outbound request boundary.

target.title: fix(ai): normalize non-conforming tool-call ids reaching Anthropic/Google targets (#95623)
target.body:
Fixes #95623

## What Problem This Solves

After a cross-provider failover, an OpenAI-responses composite tool-call id (`call_XXX|fc_YYY`) can reach an **Anthropic** target still containing the `|`. Anthropic requires tool ids matching `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, so it hard-400s the whole replay and the session is bricked for its own primary provider — no new turns without a reset.

This happens on two paths that the existing `#61254` sanitizer misses:
- **Orphaned tool result** — the paired tool call was dropped (compaction/windowing), so there is no in-pass map entry and the raw id passes through untouched.
- **Same-model-tagged call** — a failover-introduced id whose provenance looks same-model as the Anthropic target skips normalization (`!isSameModel` guard), so both the call and its result keep the `|`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`packages/ai/src/providers/transform-messages.ts` owns cross-provider tool-call-id normalization but only normalized `toolCall` ids when `!isSameModel`, and `toolResult` ids only via an in-pass `toolCallIdMap`. Non-conforming ids leaked through both gaps.

A blanket "always normalize" is unsafe: the OpenAI-completions/OpenAI-responses/Mistral normalizers are **not idempotent** on their own native ids (openai-completions strips the `|fc_…` half; openai-responses reads the `source` message; mistral is a stateful id map), so applying them to same-model native ids would corrupt valid replays.

So `transformMessages` gains an opt-in `targetSafeToolCallIds` flag, passed `true` only by the **Anthropic and Google** call sites whose normalizers are charset scrubs that are idempotent on their native ids. In target-safe mode every tool id reaching the target is normalized — the same-model call and the map-miss result included — and because the scrub is deterministic, a call and its result stay paired. Every other provider keeps the default (`false`), so their behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

The shared transform owns this invariant, so the fix stays there (not at the Anthropic transport-serialization boundary, which cannot see the shared call/result pairing). Non-goals: no change to any provider's normalizer semantics, no change to cross-provider behavior, and no id-collision hashing.

## User Impact

Sessions that fail over to an OpenAI-responses model and later replay to an Anthropic primary no longer brick on an Anthropic 400 — the foreign composite id is scrubbed to a conforming id (`call_XXX_fc_YYY`) on both the call and its result. Google targets get the same protection. OpenAI/Mistral users are unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior via the actual `transformMessages` (Anthropic target, composite id `call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01`), head `e7e315d6c5a3`:

~~~text
AFTER S1-safe orphan (targetSafe=true):          ["result:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01"]                                | PIPE-SURVIVES=false
AFTER S3-safe same-model-mistag (targetSafe=true): ["call:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01","result:call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01"] | PIPE-SURVIVES=false
REGRESSION default (targetSafe=false) same-model:  ["call:call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01","result:call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01"] | PIPE-SURVIVES=true
~~~

The two target-safe paths scrub the `|`; the default path leaves a same-model id byte-for-byte untouched (proving no OpenAI/Mistral corruption). On current `main` (target-safe absent) both S1 and S3 leak — `PIPE-SURVIVES=true`.

- `vitest run packages/ai/src/providers/transform-messages.test.ts` — 5 passed (2 red-first #95623 guards for S1/S3 + 3 regressions: default-mode composite untouched, cross-provider pair still mapped, source-requiring normalizer never invoked on a map-miss result).
- Negative control: with the source fix stashed, the S1 & S3 guard tests fail (`expected 'call_AbCd0123|fc_beef01' to be 'call_AbCd0123_fc_beef01'`) — confirms the tests guard the bug.
- Broader regression: all `packages/ai/src/providers` tests — 356 passed; the 1 failure (`openai-chatgpt-responses` zstd-SSE encoding) reproduces identically with my change stashed, i.e. pre-existing/unrelated (a zstd env issue on this host).
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` / `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` — no errors; `oxfmt --check` — clean; `check:loc` — passes (all growth in the sub-500-line transform; the three oversized provider files stay net-zero).

## Notes

- Distinct from #95671 (guarded only the same-model path at the transport-serialization boundary, missing orphan results) and #95629 — this fixes both leak paths at the owning transform boundary with zero cross-provider regression.
- AI-assisted (Claude Code); I have reviewed and understand every line.
